stories.headline: India begins talks on possible review of wheat export policy as sowing slows
stories.dek: Officials say the inter-ministerial discussions are precautionary, three months after the government lifted its ban on wheat exports, and that no move to restrict shipments has been decided.
stories.summary: India has begun inter-ministerial talks on reviewing its liberalised wheat export policy after wheat sowing fell 15.3% from a year earlier, Mint reported. A person aware of the matter said the talks are precautionary and do not signal a restriction.
body: India has started inter-ministerial discussions on a possible review of its wheat export policy, three months after it allowed unrestricted overseas shipments, Mint reported on Monday, citing two people aware of the matter.

The talks follow a slowdown in wheat sowing and concerns over soil moisture after the southwest monsoon ended with a 13% rainfall deficit this year. Agriculture ministry data showed wheat acreage at 50.07 lakh hectares as of 13 November, down 15.3% from 59.10 lakh hectares a year earlier. Officials are assessing domestic production for the crop year through June 2027.

One of the people cited said the discussions were at an initial stage and precautionary. "However, this does not mean that the government is moving towards restricting exports," the person said. The person added that because sowing is still under way, a decision would be taken "at an appropriate time" after weighing all factors and keeping farmers' interests in mind.

Queries sent to the consumer affairs, food and public distribution ministry and its department secretary had not been answered by the time Mint published. NewsBytes also reported that India may limit wheat exports after the weak monsoon and sowing slowdown.

Industry figures said exports are not currently attractive. Navneet Chitlangia, former president of the Roller Flour Millers' Federation of India, said international prices are low, partly because of a weaker dollar and a stronger rupee, and because Black Sea supplies from Russia and Ukraine are keeping global prices subdued. He said Indian prices are held up by the minimum support price.
Varun Verma, proprietor of Delhi-based Nidhiraj Exports, said his firm is not receiving enquiries from international buyers because Indian wheat is not competitively priced.

The government holds large stocks. Wheat in the central pool stood at 447.60 lakh tonnes on 1 November, against 30.727 million tonnes on 1 November 2025, according to the Food Corporation of India. For FY27 the government has allocated 21.855 million tonnes of wheat for distribution and sale, about 2.7 million tonnes more than in FY26, and has set an initial procurement target of 30.3 million tonnes for the 2026-27 marketing season, against 31.0 million tonnes last season.
keyFacts: Wheat acreage was 50.07 lakh hectares on 13 November, down 15.3% from a year earlier.
The southwest monsoon ended with a 13% rainfall deficit this year.
Central pool wheat stocks were 447.60 lakh tonnes on 1 November, FCI data show.
Initial procurement target for 2026-27 is 30.3 million tonnes, against 31.0 million tonnes last season.
India lifted its wheat export ban in August 2026.
stories.background: India banned wheat exports in 2007 and lifted the ban in September 2011. It prohibited shipments again in May 2022, eased the restriction in February 2026 and lifted the ban in August 2026. Even under the ban, it allowed limited government-to-government deals to meet diplomatic requests.
stories.whyItMatters: Any curb on exports would affect traders and flour millers who ship wheat abroad, while the government balances free foodgrain distribution commitments and buffer stocks against a possibly smaller harvest.

stories.headline: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $41 billion in cash
stories.dek: The French drugmaker gets two approved lung-disease medicines as it prepares for generic competition to Dupixent, its top-selling drug.
stories.summary: Sanofi said on Tuesday it will buy US drugmaker Insmed for $175 per share in cash, a $41 billion deal. Insmed shares closed up 14.1% at $170.15.
body: French drugmaker Sanofi said on Tuesday it will buy US company Insmed for $41 billion in cash, paying $175 per share for a firm with two approved respiratory medicines.

Insmed shares closed up 14.1% at $170.15 in the US, according to CNBC. Sanofi stock closed up 10.9% in Paris, CNBC reported. Business Standard, citing Reuters, said Sanofi was up about 6% at €90 by 0915 GMT, the top gainer on Europe's STOXX 600 index.

Business Standard reported the price is a 17.5% premium to Insmed's last closing price and 46% above its price on November 18, the day before Bloomberg News first reported Sanofi was weighing a deal. Insmed rose 24% on November 19 after that report, while Sanofi shares fell 2.9%, CNBC said.

The acquisition covers Brinsupri, a treatment for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, and Arikayce, which treats refractory mycobacterium avium complex lung disease. It also includes a drug in Phase 3 trials, STAT reported. Sanofi will pay with a combination of debt and cash on hand and said it has committed financing.

Sanofi expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027 and to add to earnings per share by the end of 2028. Finance chief François Roger said annual cost benefits would exceed $500 million. JPMorgan was Sanofi's exclusive financial adviser.

Chief executive Belen Garijo, who took over in May, said the two medicines have combined peak sales potential expected to exceed $10 billion through the end of the next decade. Jefferies analysts forecast 2035 sales of $6.8 billion for Brinsupri and $1.3 billion for Arikayce.

Dupixent, an eczema and inflammation drug, generated sales of over €15 billion last year, almost 40% of Sanofi's total, according to Business Standard. Jefferies expects it to lose exclusivity in 2031–32.

Analysts were broadly positive. Barclays called the deal a "breath of fresh air". Jefferies said: "The deal does not fix Sanofi's R&D/pipeline questions, but it buys time." It flagged possible future competition from AstraZeneca's tozorakimab, which is being studied in bronchiectasis.
Claus Henrik Johansen of Global Health Invest, a Sanofi shareholder, said more clinical data and sales projections were needed to support the valuation.
Roger said Sanofi will keep room for smaller acquisitions, particularly early-stage assets in immunology, rare diseases and vaccines.

Belen Garijo, formerly CEO of Merck KGaA, replaced Paul Hudson at Sanofi after the board chose not to renew his mandate. CNBC said his costly emphasis on R&D failed to deliver speedy results. Hudson joined Insmed's board in October, Business Standard reported.

CNBC said the deal is the largest in the industry since Pfizer bought Seagen for $43 billion in December 2023. Business Standard described it as Sanofi's biggest in two decades.
stories.whyItMatters: Sanofi relies on Dupixent for almost 40% of sales, and the drug is expected to face generic competition in 2031–32. The purchase adds respiratory products intended to offset that loss.

stories.headline: Yamuna Expressway speed limit cut to 75 kmph from November 25 for fog season
stories.dek: The authority has told concessionaire Jaypee Infratech to replace worn reflective tape and install fog lights, as forecasts point to fog over several northern states.
stories.summary: The maximum speed on the Yamuna Expressway falls from 100 kmph to 75 kmph from November 25 to February 15, an official statement said. Headlines on IMD forecasts point to dense fog across eight states and rain alerts.
body: The maximum speed limit on the Yamuna Expressway will be cut from 100 kmph to 75 kmph for the period from November 25 to February 15, to reduce fog-related accidents, an official statement said on Tuesday.

The authority has directed the expressway's concessionaire, Jaypee Infratech Limited, to put the lower limit and additional safety measures into effect immediately. The statement said the aim is to alert motorists to take care in low visibility and to minimise the risk of accidents.

The revised limit will be displayed prominently at key locations, with information boards at various points and notices in newspapers. Pamphlets on safe driving in fog will be handed out at entry and exit points, toll plazas and roadside facilities. Toll plazas will make public announcements, FM radio channels will broadcast advisories, and large electronic display boards will carry instructions.

The authority also flagged technical problems. It said the brightness and reflectivity of reflective tapes at several locations have deteriorated, which could leave road markings and warning signs hard to see. It ordered the immediate replacement of damaged tapes and directed that fog lights be installed at the entry and exit points.
Traffic on the expressway generally rises on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. The authority has asked for effective arrangements at toll plazas to keep vehicles moving smoothly on those days.

On the wider weather picture, headlines from News On AIR and News24Online on Tuesday said the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had forecast dense fog across eight states, including Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, along with rain alerts and winds of up to 60 km. The full IMD bulletins were not available for this report, so rainfall and temperature figures could not be confirmed.
The authority has asked the concerned agency to carry out all the instructions and submit a compliance report.
keyFacts: Speed limit on the Yamuna Expressway falls from 100 kmph to 75 kmph.
The lower limit applies from November 25 to February 15.
Jaypee Infratech Limited is the expressway's concessionaire and must comply immediately.
Damaged reflective tapes are to be replaced and fog lights installed at entry and exit points.
Headlines cite an IMD forecast of dense fog across eight states.
stories.background: Dense fog in winter reduces visibility on expressways and raises the risk of accidents, which the authority cited as the reason for the seasonal speed reduction.
stories.whyItMatters: Motorists on the Yamuna Expressway must drive at no more than 75 kmph for about twelve weeks, with traffic expected to be heaviest on weekends and holidays.

stories.headline: Tidal to ban fully AI-generated music from December 9, remove millions of tracks
stories.dek: The streaming service says 43% of tracks uploaded in the past 90 days were detected as AI-generated, and that earlier labelling and demonetising did not deter submissions.
stories.summary: Tidal said on Tuesday it will start rejecting and removing music made wholly by artificial intelligence on December 9. Songs made with AI assistance will still be accepted.
body: Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will ban music generated entirely by artificial intelligence, rejecting new uploads and deleting existing tracks from December 9.

Sources differ on how many tracks will go. Tidal's figures, as reported by TechCrunch and The Verge, put the removals at more than 29 million, or around 29 million, by the end of the year. TechCrunch and Rolling Stone also cited a figure of 27 million tracks, about 6.3% of the catalogue, as fully AI-generated. Rolling Stone reported a range of 27 to 29 million.

Robert Anderson, who leads Tidal's music operations, said on X that 43% of tracks distributed to the platform in the past 90 days were detected as AI-generated. He said the company expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day under the new policy. The Verge spelled his surname Andersen.

Tidal said 96% of the AI-generated songs it has identified received no streams. "It's true that not all songs catch on immediately, and artists should have time to build their fanbases. But this situation is different – at this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried," the company said in a post.

The ban also covers distributors, the companies that deliver songs from artists and labels to streaming services. Tidal said they may not deliver fully AI-generated tracks, and it will reject deliveries whose metadata, the descriptive data attached to a file, says the music was made solely with AI tools. The company is using detection software from Ircam Amplify to identify such songs.
Tracks made with help from AI tools remain allowed, as long as AI is not the sole output. Rolling Stone said the policy targets music made completely with tools such as Suno, Lyria and Udio.

Tidal began tagging and demonetising wholly AI-generated tracks in June. Anderson said on X that this was not enough. Rolling Stone reported he described Tidal as the first streaming platform to ban AI music and urged others to "follow suit". TechCrunch described it as one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to do so.

Tidal said it has already removed more than 65,000 tracks flagged for suspected artist-name impersonation. In a statement it said wholly AI-generated music meant to mislead listeners "diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans".

A Tidal spokesperson told Rolling Stone that most appeals against its AI flags had been upheld on review. The spokesperson said a small number of false positives was inevitable. Rolling Stone noted that distributor DistroKid accidentally removed real artists' music earlier this year during mass takedowns tied to a lawsuit by Universal Music Group.

Other services have taken different routes. Deezer will add a toggle for users to filter out AI music, while Spotify and YouTube Music label such tracks. Tidal said all fully AI-generated tracks will be gone by the start of 2027, according to Rolling Stone.
keyFacts: Tidal's ban on fully AI-generated music takes effect on December 9.
43% of tracks uploaded in the past 90 days were detected as AI-generated, Tidal said.
Tidal expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day.
Tidal said 96% of the AI tracks it identified have no streams.
AI-assisted songs remain allowed if AI is not the sole output.
stories.background: Tidal began labelling and demonetising wholly AI-generated tracks in June. Bandcamp banned AI music earlier this year. Spotify, YouTube Music and Apple Music have opted for labels, and Deezer is adding a user filter.
stories.whyItMatters: Tidal says AI uploads divert streams and royalties from human artists and bury their work. Artists whose music is wrongly flagged can appeal, the company says.

stories.headline: Meta launches Muse AI agent in UK, with regulators watching closely
stories.dek: The ICO and the CMA said Meta had agreed to monitoring and changes to its terms before the launch, and both said they would act if they have concerns.
stories.summary: Meta launched its Muse AI agent in the UK on Tuesday, letting users hand it tasks such as shopping and booking travel. The UK's data and competition regulators said they were in talks with Meta and would monitor the rollout.
body: Meta launched its Muse AI agent, an assistant that can carry out tasks such as shopping and booking travel on a user's behalf, in the UK on Tuesday, with two UK regulators saying they would monitor the rollout.

Muse works as an app or inside WhatsApp. Users can give it a name, a look and a personality, and assign jobs such as sending an email, booking travel or buying presents. Meta said Muse cannot buy anything or send an email without the user's permission, and connects only to apps the user allows.

Meta said Muse cannot see people's passwords or payment methods and does not share conversations with advertisers. A separate "security agent" checks Muse's actions against the permissions granted, the company said. According to The Guardian, Meta has signed deals with British businesses including Marks & Spencer, Currys, Sainsbury's and easyJet. Where a company has no "connector" app, which is a direct link between the agent and a company's systems, Muse uses its website instead.

The Information Commissioner's Office, the UK data protection regulator, said Meta had committed to a "voluntary monitoring and reporting scheme". The Competition and Markets Authority said its talks had led to changes making the app's terms and conditions "fairer".
"We will be closely monitoring this and if we have concerns we will not hesitate to act to protect UK consumers," said Sarah Cardell, the CMA's chief executive.

Reuters reported last week that Meta employees had raised concerns about Muse's performance. In one case a staff member received a reminder to reply to a message on Signal, a different messaging app. In another, Muse sent a message containing random bank account balances. Meta said internal testing allows it to add safety and privacy protections before public release. The Guardian reported it is understood most of the problems Reuters flagged stemmed from a bug that has been fixed.
Muse runs on Muse Spark, the first model from Meta's "super intelligence" AI lab. The Guardian reported that Muse is ranked first on Google's free app store and second on Apple's in the US.

Separately on Tuesday, Meta said Instagram users can chat with Muse inside direct messages, TechCrunch reported. Users can share posts and ask it to add a coffee shop to an itinerary or find a Black Friday deal. The feature is rolling out on iOS and Android in the US, Canada, Mexico, Japan and Singapore. Meta said nothing is shared, published or sent without approval.

Walmart also announced on Tuesday that customers can shop its Black Friday deals through Muse. Users sign in to their Walmart account, and Walmart said Muse does not get access to shopping history or other personal information. Shoppers can set spending limits and require approval before purchases.
keyFacts: Meta launched Muse in the UK on Tuesday, as an app and inside WhatsApp.
The ICO said Meta committed to a voluntary monitoring and reporting scheme.
The CMA said talks led to "fairer" terms and conditions for the app.

stories.whyItMatters: UK users of Muse will be handing an AI agent access to their email, calendars and shopping apps, and the ICO and CMA say they will monitor how Meta handles privacy and consumer protection.

stories.headline: OpenAI says GPT-6 models can design proteins without specialised biology tools
stories.dek: In a preprint, the company reports lab tests with partner Onava found evidence of binding for designs across five targets, though specialised models still helped select candidates.
stories.summary: OpenAI published a preprint claiming its GPT-6 models can design protein structures and sequences using only reasoning and general-purpose code. Lab tests with Onava showed evidence of binding for at least one protein at each of five targets.
body: OpenAI said on November 24 that its GPT-6 family of AI models can design new proteins using only reasoning and general-purpose code, without calling specialised biology models to generate the designs, according to a preprint and an accompanying post from the company.

The preprint is titled "GPT-6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models". A preprint is a research paper released before independent peer review. The findings below are OpenAI's own account.

OpenAI said an internal research model matched or outperformed specialised models on many protein design tasks. Newer model generations improved on many of the 14 protein tasks tested. The company said predicting a complete protein structure remained a clear weakness.

Researchers could steer designs through prompts, OpenAI said, for example by marking where a small protein called a minibinder should attach to its target and how many coils or strands it should contain. The company said an internal model followed such instructions with near-perfect fidelity.

OpenAI also tested designs in a lab with its research partner, Onava. Onava made small proteins based on three-dimensional structures designed by a pre-release version of GPT-6.2. For each of five chosen targets, at least one protein showed evidence of binding, meaning it attached to the target.

The lab work was not free of specialised tools. A specialised model called SolubleMPNN suggested the amino acid sequences, the chains of chemical building blocks that determine how a protein folds. Other specialised models helped pick candidates predicted to fold as designed and bind at the intended site.

In a computational comparison against RFdiffusion, a specialised protein-design model, GPT-6.2's three-dimensional designs scored slightly lower, OpenAI said. Its latest internal models scored higher.

In separate experiments, GPT-6.2 designed new sequences for existing minibinders and antibodies. After candidate selection with specialised models, many of the redesigned proteins still bound the same targets as the originals, the company said.

OpenAI said the models' written reasoning and code suggest they draw on mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology. In one example, a design aimed at the immune-related protein IL-7Rα, the model proposed how the two proteins might interact, then wrote and ran code to explore shapes and amino acid choices.
keyFacts: OpenAI published the GPT-6 protein-design preprint on November 24.
Lab partner Onava tested designs from a pre-release GPT-6.2.
At least one protein bound each of five chosen targets.
Specialised models supplied sequences and helped select candidates for lab testing.
GPT-6.2 scored slightly below RFdiffusion in computational design quality, OpenAI said.
stories.background: Proteins are chains of amino acids that fold into three-dimensional shapes, and the shape influences what a protein does. Specialised AI models that generate protein structures and sequences have made design more practical, OpenAI said, but they need substantial expertise to use and coordinate, and each accepts only particular kinds of input.
stories.whyItMatters: If the results hold up, researchers could use plain-language prompts with one general model instead of coordinating several specialised tools. The claims have not yet been peer reviewed.

stories.headline: India's AI startups raise $1.6 billion in nine months, up 96%, Tracxn says
stories.dek: Mumbai overtook Bengaluru as the largest recipient of AI funding, while deal numbers fell and about 90% of capital came from 10 rounds.
stories.summary: AI companies in India raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in the first nine months of 2026, 96% more than a year earlier, according to data platform Tracxn. Deal volumes fell, and a few large rounds accounted for most of the money.
body: AI companies in India raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in the first nine months of 2026, a 96% increase on the same period of 2025, according to a report by the data intelligence platform Tracxn.

The report places India ninth among countries for AI funding in the period. India accounted for 0.4% of the money raised by AI companies globally, behind the US, China, the UK, France, Singapore, Germany, Australia and Canada.

The rise came from a small number of large deals. The number of deals fell from 149 in the first nine months of 2025 to 87 in the same period of 2026, while the average deal size more than tripled to $18.5 million from $5.5 million. Around 90% of the total capital was raised in just 10 rounds, the report shows.

The largest round was by Neysa, a Mumbai-based AI cloud provider, which raised $600 million in a Series B round in February. A Series B is a later stage of fundraising, after a company's first outside investments. Sarvam, a Bengaluru-based generative AI developer, raised $255 million in a Series B in June and a further $90.4 million in August. Yotta raised $150 million in a Series D in July.

By stage, early-stage funding rose 191% and late-stage funding rose 4%, while seed-stage funding, the earliest outside investment, fell 42%. Tracxn said this suggests investors are favouring companies with more mature business models and technology. It also said the fall in deal numbers and seed funding indicates growth is concentrated among a few companies rather than broad-based.

Mumbai overtook Bengaluru as the largest recipient of AI funding in the country. Mumbai's AI funding rose from $15.7 million in the first nine months of 2025, a 2% share, to $765 million in the same period of 2026, a 48% share.

Bengaluru-based AI companies raised $711 million, giving the city a 44% share of total AI funding. Its share was 54% a year earlier. Tracxn named Sarvam and Emergent as having the largest rounds in the city.
keyFacts: AI companies in India raised $1.6 billion in nine months of 2026, up 96% year on year.
Deals fell to 87 from 149; average deal size rose to $18.5 million from $5.5 million.
Neysa's $600 million Series B in February was the largest round.
Mumbai raised $765 million (48% share); Bengaluru raised $711 million (44%).
India ranks ninth globally, with 0.4% of AI funding raised worldwide.
stories.background: Tracxn is a data intelligence platform that tracks startup funding. Its report covers equity funding raised by AI companies from January to September 2026 and compares it with the same months of 2025.
stories.whyItMatters: The figures show AI investment in India is rising but concentrated in a few companies, with seed-stage funding for the youngest startups falling 42%.

stories.headline: China launches Shenzhou-24 carrying Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to Tiangong
stories.dek: Ali, a former Pakistani air force pilot, is the first foreign national China has sent to space, flying as a payload specialist for about a week.
stories.summary: A Long March 2F rocket was scheduled to lift Shenzhou-24 from Jiuquan at 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on November 25, carrying Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. He is the first foreigner China has launched to space.
body: China scheduled the launch of its Shenzhou-24 mission for 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Wednesday, November 25, carrying Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreign national China has sent into space, to its Tiangong station.

A Long March 2F rocket was set to lift off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, according to Space.com, which carried China Central Television's live broadcast. The report was published before liftoff.

Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, will be the first Pakistani to reach orbit. He flies as a payload specialist alongside commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi. Space.com noted that Namira Salim flew on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in October 2023, making her the first Pakistani to travel to space.

Tang has flown on Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17, launched in June 2021 and October 2023. The state-run Xinhua news agency said he will become the first person to visit Tiangong three times. Shenzhou-24 is Wu's first spaceflight.

Tang and Wu are expected to stay aboard for six months, the usual rotation. Ali will remain for about a week, then return to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 crew, which launched on May 24.

The South China Morning Post reported that the third Shenzhou-23 member, Zhu Yangzhu, will stay on the station until Shenzhou-24 returns. That would make Zhu the first Chinese astronaut to spend a year in orbit.
China announced the crew on Monday night, November 23. Space.com said Beijing generally does not name Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch.
Shenzhou-24 is China's 18th crewed spaceflight and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali is the first foreign national China has launched to space.
Ali is due to stay in orbit about a week.
Commander Tang Hongbo is to become the first person to visit Tiangong three times.
Zhu Yangzhu is to spend a year in orbit, a first for a Chinese astronaut.
stories.background: China and Pakistan signed a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad in February 2025. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who travelled to China for training. Tiangong is a three-module station that China finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022.
stories.whyItMatters: The flight opens Tiangong to a foreign astronaut for the first time and gives Pakistan its first person in orbit.

stories.headline: ICMR survey finds 55.9% of women aged 15-49 anaemic, 65% of adolescents low in B12
stories.dek: The SAMPADA survey also reports lower anaemia prevalence than NFHS-5 in several groups, though the Times of India says the two surveys are not directly comparable.
stories.summary: A national ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition survey found anaemia in 55.9 per cent of non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49. Vitamin B12 deficiency affects about two-thirds of adolescents, and iron deficiency accompanied only some anaemia cases.
body: More than half of Indian women aged 15-49 are anaemic, according to the SAMPADA survey of the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition, which found a prevalence of 55.9 per cent among non-pregnant, non-lactating women in that age group.

The survey ran from 2023 to 2025. It covered more than two lakh people in 183 districts across 35 states and union territories, drawing on over 81,000 households and more than 1.7 lakh blood samples, The Times of India reported.

The data fill a gap in the NFHS-6 fact sheets released earlier this year, which carried no anaemia estimates. The government had said those figures would come from an independent ICMR survey using venous blood samples rather than finger-prick tests, according to the sources.

Among other groups, anaemia affected 46.3 per cent of adolescent girls and 22.8 per cent of adolescent boys aged 10-19. It was found in 41.8 per cent of children aged 12-59 months and 31.3 per cent of those aged 5-9 years. The rate was 43.6 per cent among pregnant women, 58.1 per cent among lactating women and 22 per cent among men aged 20-59.

Andaman and Nicobar recorded the highest prevalence among non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49, at 81.2 per cent. The Times of India said state-wise estimates showed sharp regional differences.
Vitamin B12 deficiency was found in 65.4 per cent of adolescent girls and 66.1 per cent of adolescent boys. It affected 57.4 per cent of women of reproductive age and 60.4 per cent of men aged 20-59.

Iron deficiency accompanied anaemia in only 27 per cent of adolescent girls and women of reproductive age. Iron deficiency itself affected 36.3 per cent of adolescent girls, 34.1 per cent of women of reproductive age and 10 per cent of adolescent boys.

The Hindu, citing data from the Union Health Ministry, reported that SAMPADA shows lower prevalence than NFHS-5 in several groups. It put the figure for children at 41.8 per cent against 64 per cent earlier, for pregnant women at 44 per cent against 52 per cent, and for men at 19 per cent against 25 per cent. The Times of India reported the men's figure as 22 per cent for ages 20-59.

The Times of India said comparisons with NFHS-5, which reported 57 per cent for women aged 15-49, are not direct because the surveys covered different groups of women and used different testing methods.

Dr Tulika Seth, professor of haematology at AIIMS, said not all anaemia stems from nutritional deficiency. "Iron supplements alone will not help these patients," she said, citing conditions such as thalassaemia, sickle cell disease, tuberculosis and cancer. She said her team has been working with the Anaemia Mukt Bharat programme on simple algorithms to identify such cases.
keyFacts: Anaemia found in 55.9 per cent of non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49.
B12 deficiency affects 65.4 per cent of adolescent girls and 66.1 per cent of adolescent boys.
Andaman and Nicobar has the highest prevalence among women aged 15-49, at 81.2 per cent.
Survey analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from 183 districts.
stories.background: India stopped publishing anaemia data in the NFHS series after its fifth round. The NFHS-6 fact sheets omitted anaemia estimates, and the government said they would come from a separate ICMR survey based on venous blood samples.
stories.whyItMatters: The findings indicate that iron supplementation alone may not address anaemia, as B12 deficiency and other conditions also contribute, according to the survey data and AIIMS haematologist Dr Tulika Seth.

stories.headline: Bisleri says FSSAI action covers one Goa batch, no longer on sale
stories.dek: The company says retesting found bromate within limits, but acknowledges one of six samples showed PAHs at 0.144 micrograms per litre.
stories.summary: Bisleri International said on Tuesday that the FSSAI's sale prohibition applies only to batch GO 270, made in Goa in September 2025 and no longer in the market. The regulator has sanctioned prosecution and plans wider testing of packaged water brands.
body: Bisleri International said on Tuesday that the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's action concerns a single batch made at its Goa plant on September 27, 2025, which it says is no longer in the market.

The company said the sale prohibition applies only to batch GO 270. "Bisleri produces more than 50,000 batches annually," it said. It added that all 143 of its plants remain operational and that the Goa facility has received no suspension order.

Bisleri said FSSAI clarified on November 23 that bromate was below the permissible limit on re-testing of the batch sample. It acknowledged that one of six samples tested in a later round showed polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) at 0.144 micrograms per litre. Another sample from the same batch cleared all parameters.

The regulator had said on Sunday that it sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri after a sample was declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. It said the sample failed on bromate and, at a referral laboratory, on PAHs.

On Monday FSSAI said the referral lab's report is final when a food business operator appeals. It said the prohibition order covered only batch GO 270, "Only one batch was found to be non-compliant," and that Bisleri had been asked to conduct a root cause analysis.

Bisleri's account of the testing differs in detail. It said FSSAI drew six samples in Goa on September 30, 2025. Five passed, and the sixth showed bromate at 12 micrograms per litre against a limit of 10. It appealed in November 2025 and the referral lab found bromate within the limit but flagged PAHs.

The company said it then had the sample tested at an FSSAI-approved lab, which also found bromate within the limit, and sent the results to FSSAI's Western Regional Office in February. It said it received no further communication and understood the matter to be closed. It also said it had sought a PAH retest in February 2026.
Bisleri said no subsequent samples tested by FSSAI across its plants had shown adverse PAH findings. It said it would consider legal action over what it called false and misleading claims.

Firstpost reported that FSSAI plans to test more samples nationwide and inspect other brands. Goa's Food and Drugs Administration director, Shweta S Dessai, has instructed officials to collect samples of packaged water brands made and sold in the state.

stories.whyItMatters: FSSAI has signalled wider testing of packaged water brands, and state officials in Goa and Gujarat have begun or announced sampling and inspections of producers.

stories.headline: Kala-azar cases surface in Uttarakhand, which is outside India's endemic zone
stories.dek: Records obtained under the RTI Act show AIIMS Delhi treated 33 patients from the state between 2016 and 2025, while state data lists two cases.
stories.summary: Mongabay India reports that kala-azar, a sandfly-borne disease, is appearing in Uttarakhand, including among people who had not travelled to endemic areas. State health records show far fewer cases than hospital registers in Delhi.
body: Kala-azar is being diagnosed in Uttarakhand, a state outside India's endemic zone, including in residents with no travel history to affected areas, Mongabay India reported on Tuesday. Records from Delhi hospitals show far more cases than the state has logged.

Records obtained through a Right to Information request show the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi, received kala-azar patients from Uttarakhand every year from 2016 to 2025, 33 in all. In response to a separate RTI request, the state's National Health Mission reported two cases in 2017 and none from 2018 to 2025.

The report attributes the gap to how data is compiled. Uttarakhand's health mission collects figures through frontline workers, with records moving up from primary and community health centres to district and state hospitals. AIIMS keeps its own registers, so a patient from Uttarakhand treated in Delhi can appear there without appearing in state records.

The report centres on Chair Talla, a village at 1,100 metres in Pauri district, which recorded what was believed to be the state's last known case nine years ago. Bhupendra Chauhan fell ill there in December 2013. A bone marrow test at PGIMER, Chandigarh, confirmed visceral leishmaniasis. He relapsed after treatment, and his brother Sunil said the family visited at least four hospitals and spent more than ₹12-13 lakh.

Another villager, Ramesh Singh, was diagnosed at AIIMS Rishikesh in 2021, relapsed and died in December 2022, leaving debts of roughly ₹5 lakh, the report said. Ramesh does not appear in state records. Chauhan's case, one of the two the state did record, is entered under an incorrect date.
Sunil said he pressed the Pauri chief medical officer's office and later the World Health Organization for action. The state health mission sent a team to the village in 2017.

Doctors at AIIMS Rishikesh documented seven cases between 2017 and 2019 among residents of high-altitude Uttarakhand, none of whom had travelled to an endemic area. The findings were published in 2020 in the Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care.

Kala-azar is endemic to Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh. A study estimates 165.4 million people are at risk across 54 districts, the report said. It cites changing environmental conditions, livestock as possible sandfly hosts and the spread of sandflies to higher elevations as open questions about transmission.
keyFacts: AIIMS Delhi received 33 kala-azar patients from Uttarakhand between 2016 and 2025, per RTI records.
Uttarakhand's health mission reported two cases in 2017 and none from 2018 to 2025.
AIIMS Rishikesh documented seven cases in high-altitude residents between 2017 and 2019.
Untreated kala-azar has a reported mortality rate of 75%.
stories.background: Kala-azar, or visceral leishmaniasis, is a parasitic disease spread by the bites of infected female sandflies. Symptoms include prolonged fever, enlarged organs, anaemia and weight loss, and can take months to appear. Insecticide spraying nearly eliminated it in the 1950s, but it resurged in 1974, spreading from four districts in Bihar to parts of Jharkhand, West Bengal and eastern Uttar Pradesh.
stories.whyItMatters: Cases diagnosed outside Uttarakhand are missing from state records, which obscures the extent of local transmission. The report says gaps in surveillance and vector control could undermine elimination gains, particularly in states without dedicated programmes.

stories.headline: ISRO targets December for first operational SSLV launch
stories.dek: The agency needs two successful development flights before declaring the rocket operational; it has completed three, one of which fell short of its intended orbit.
stories.summary: ISRO is aiming to launch another SSLV mission in December, a senior official said. The year has seen far fewer launches than planned after two PSLV failures, with only three achieved against a target of 17 for FY 2026-27.
body: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is aiming to launch another Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) mission in December, a senior ISRO official told The Indian Express, as the agency looks to close a year of reduced launch activity.

The agency needs two successful development missions before a launcher is declared operational. SSLV has flown three development flights. The first, on August 7, 2022, did not place its satellites in the intended orbit. The second, in February 2023, and the third, in August 2024, were declared successful.

ISRO's annual report planned 17 launches for FY 2026-27, including at least four PSLV and five SSLV missions. The agency has achieved three this year, including the failed PSLV-C62. It launched the earth observation satellite EOS-5 in September and the navigation satellite NVS-03 in October, which brought the country's navigation system back online.

The PSLV failed twice, with PSLV-C61 in May 2025 and PSLV-C62 in January 2026. Both failures were due to anomalies in the third stage, and ISRO has said the causes differed. The third-stage configuration was revisited, with changes to design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures and quality checks. The design was strengthened and the nozzle configuration improved.

ISRO chairman V Narayanan told The Indian Express on the sidelines of the 5th India International Space Conclave in New Delhi that one ground test has been completed. "We have already conducted one ground test and will be ready to launch the PSLV after another ground test," he said.

The privately built PSLV-N1 may have to wait until after ISRO's own PSLV flies, The Indian Express reported on Monday. Narayanan said on Tuesday that the industry-built rocket would launch in the first quarter of 2027. The Times of India reported he said a consortium of L&T and HAL has been given five PSLVs to build. ISRO's commercial arm NSIL signed a Rs 860 crore contract with the consortium in September 2022.

Narayanan also said the Gaganyaan mission is not late. "We are in the final phase. The rocket and other items are ready. We're working on the orbital module," he said, adding that it will launch at the earliest opportunity.
keyFacts: ISRO aims to launch another SSLV mission in December 2026.
SSLV has flown three development flights: August 2022, February 2023 and August 2024.
ISRO achieved three launches this year against 17 planned for FY 2026-27.
PSLV-N1, built by an L&T and HAL consortium, is targeted for the first quarter of 2027.
NSIL's contract with the consortium for five PSLVs is worth Rs 860 crore.
stories.background: The PSLV, ISRO's workhorse rocket, failed in May 2025 and January 2026 because of third-stage anomalies. ISRO changed the stage's design and quality processes and has completed one ground test, with another planned before the next PSLV flight.
stories.whyItMatters: An operational SSLV would give India a declared small-satellite launcher, while the PSLV return to flight and the private PSLV-N1 depend on further ground testing.

stories.headline: GTA VI posts record first-day sales of about $3.7 billion worldwide
stories.dek: PS5 consoles have sold out across Singapore, while Take-Two has issued takedown notices against a fan project to run a leaked Xbox build of the game on PC.
stories.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI, released on November 19, made a record US$3.79 billion in first-day sales worldwide, according to CNA. Take-Two has meanwhile targeted a PC recompilation project built on a leaked Xbox build.
body: Grand Theft Auto VI made a record US$3.79 billion in worldwide sales on its first day, CNA reported, after Rockstar Games released the title on November 19. BigGo Finance put the figure at approximately $3.7 billion.

It is the first new game in the series in 13 years. It is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and Series S. No PC version has been announced, and CNA said there is no official release window for one.

In Singapore, shops have run out of PS5 consoles. CNA reported that retailers of all sizes confirmed the sell-out, and that Sony's Singapore website showed backorders unavailable on Tuesday. Courts said new stock is expected towards the end of December. One shopper told CNA that a Sony staff member had said the console would be restocked in January.

Retailers linked the demand to the game. Michael Ong, manager of RPG Right Place for Gadgets in Paya Lebar, said stock flew off the shelves once the game was released. GameMartz managing director Lim Kok Wee said console demand had risen five times compared with normal days. Qisahn's owner, Soon Qishan, said his store sold out on the night of November 10.

In India, The Hindu reported that the game costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox. Rockstar sells it as a download, including in boxes in stores. Blinkit offered a collectible box containing a download code in select areas of 11 cities. Companies including boAt and Inde by ChairsCarte gave staff a day off.

On the PC front, The Verge reported that Take-Two sent a DMCA takedown notice against Leonida, a project by a 15-year-old who goes by "NotRexed". Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows.

Take-Two's enforcement team targeted the project's main GitHub repository and more than 2,900 forks. The notice claimed the project "infringes upon Take-Two's copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI."

A leaker known as Cyberleek published a full Xbox build earlier this week, according to The Verge. Other efforts, including the VIctory project, are trying to get the game running on PC. The Verge said recent reports suggest an official PC version could arrive in a few months.
keyFacts: GTA VI made a record US$3.79 billion in first-day sales, per CNA.
The game launched on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
India prices are ₹5,999 (Standard) and ₹7,499 (Ultimate).
Take-Two's takedown targeted Leonida's main repository and more than 2,900 forks.
Courts expects new Singapore PS5 stock towards the end of December.
stories.background: Grand Theft Auto V was released in September 2013, and the sequel's arrival ended a wait of more than 13 years. Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA VI; GTA V reached PC in 2015, as The Hindu noted.
stories.whyItMatters: Console buyers in Singapore face shortages until at least late December, and PC players have no official version of the game yet.

stories.headline: Sooryavanshi, 15, hits 204 off 53 balls as India A beat UAE by seven wickets
stories.dek: The left-hander struck 28 sixes, the most in a List A innings, and reached 100 in 28 balls and 200 in 52 in the Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha.
stories.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 204 off 53 balls for India A against the UAE on Tuesday, setting List A records for the fastest hundred, the fastest double century and most sixes. India A chased 250 in 14.2 overs.
body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 204 off 53 balls for India A against the UAE in Doha on Tuesday, setting List A records for the fastest hundred and double century and for most sixes in an innings, as India A won by seven wickets.

India A chased down a target of 250 in 14.2 overs in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament, finishing on 254 for 3 with 214 balls remaining. Sooryavanshi hit seven fours and 28 sixes, a strike rate of 384.90, and was named Player of the Match. He scored 204 of India A's 254 runs.

He reached his hundred off 28 balls, one fewer than the 29 taken by Australia's Jake Fraser-McGurk in 2023. His 150 came off 40 balls, bettering his own previous mark of 59 balls, set for Bihar against Arunachal Pradesh last year. His 200 came off 52 balls. The previous fastest was 103 balls, by Chad Bowes for Canterbury against Otago in 2024.
The 28 sixes broke the List A record of 23 held by D'Arcy Short, set against Queensland in 2018. The International Cricket Council confirmed the records, ABC News reported.

Sooryavanshi began the chase with two dot balls, then hit three successive sixes off Zahid Ali and reached fifty off 16 balls. India A were 100 after five overs. He was dropped on 163 and missed by the wicketkeeper on 76, when a stumping chance went begging.
He was out in the 13th over, caught at long-off while going for another six, with India A five runs short of victory. Rinku Singh finished unbeaten on 27.

India A captain Tilak Varma said: "No words to say for him. I would only say it's like absolute carnage." He added: "First five overs the match was done, five overs we are 100 and the way he carried on after that, it was tremendous to watch."

UAE had made 249 for 8 after choosing to bat. Harpreet Singh scored a career-best List A 130 off 144 balls. Arshad Khan took 4 for 43 for India A. Ibrar Ahmad conceded 71 runs in three overs and did not bowl again.
The win took India A into the semifinals of the tournament, according to The Hindu.
keyFacts: Sooryavanshi scored 204 off 53 balls, including 28 sixes and seven fours.
His hundred took 28 balls; Jake Fraser-McGurk's record was 29 balls.
His double century took 52 balls; Chad Bowes's record was 103 balls.
India A made 254 for 3, beating UAE by seven wickets with 214 balls left.
Harpreet Singh made 130 for UAE, who scored 249 for 8.
stories.background: Sooryavanshi already held the record for the fastest List A fifty, off 11 balls against Sri Lanka A earlier this year. It was his second List A century in 16 innings. In July he became India's youngest men's international on his T20I debut against England in Manchester, passing Sachin Tendulkar's record. He scored 776 runs for Rajasthan Royals in this year's IPL, the tournament's highest, at a strike rate of 237.30, and made 175 in the Under-19 World Cup final in February, according to ABC and The Guardian.
stories.whyItMatters: The innings put India A in the semifinals of the Asia Cup Rising Stars and rewrote several List A batting records.

stories.headline: Gukesh holds Sindarov to 38-move draw in world championship opener
stories.dek: The defending champion spent more than 36 minutes on one move and fell short on the clock, but defended a queenless ending with Black in Geneva.
stories.summary: D. Gukesh drew Game 1 of the world chess championship against Javokhir Sindarov by repetition after 38 moves in Cologny, Geneva, on Tuesday. He plays White in Game 2 on Wednesday.
body: Defending champion D. Gukesh of India drew the opening game of the world chess championship against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov by repetition after 38 moves at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, near Geneva, on Tuesday.

Gukesh, playing Black, chose the Berlin Defence of the Ruy Lopez, an opening The Indian Express said he rarely uses. The queens came off on the eighth move, according to The Guardian. Sindarov moved quickly early on, then took more than 22 minutes over his 14th move, the Express reported.

Gukesh spent more than 36 minutes on a single move, The Guardian said, and fell well behind on the clock. Sportstar's live coverage recorded him with less than five minutes and eight moves left to make before the time control at move 40. The broadcast win probabilities at one stage showed 31 per cent for Sindarov, 57 per cent for a draw and 12 per cent for Gukesh.
The game reached a same-coloured-bishop ending, according to Sportstar. Play settled into repetition from move 33, with Rg5+ Kh7 and Rh5 Kg8 repeated until move 38.

The finish had a twist. Sindarov claimed the draw one move too early, the Express reported, and the arbiter added time to Gukesh's clock. Sportstar and the Express put the penalty at one minute; The Guardian's report said two. Sindarov made a valid claim on the next cycle.

Gukesh said the time he invested early helped him later. "When I got into the time trouble, I'd already thought about the next few moves," he said. "And then the moves after that were pretty easy." He said he was never worried and became "a little optimistic" around 31...Bc3.

Sindarov called Gukesh's 27...Kf6 "super strong" and said he had underestimated the safety of the king there. "But in general, I understand my position is very close to equal," he said. "I'm trying to keep finding some interesting ideas, but then he defended very well."
Gukesh will have White in Game 2 on Wednesday, with the score level at 0.5–0.5. Games start at 7.30pm India time.
keyFacts: Game 1 ended in a draw by repetition after 38 moves on Tuesday.
Gukesh had Black; Sindarov had White and made the first move.
The match is best of 14 games, with a $2.5m prize fund.
The first player to reach 7½ points wins the title.
Game 2 is on Wednesday, with Gukesh playing White.
stories.background: Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world champion in December 2024 by beating China's Ding Liren, after losing Game 1 of that match. The Indian Express reported he won 13 and lost 16 of 54 classical games in the past 12 months and is ranked No. 26. Sindarov, also 20, won this year's Candidates tournament and arrived unbeaten in his last 69 classical games, the Express said.
stories.whyItMatters: Drawing with Black against the in-form challenger leaves the match level, with Gukesh holding White in Game 2.

stories.headline: CAS sets aside CAF ruling and restores Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations champions
stories.dek: A three-member panel unanimously held that the referee's decision to resume the final was covered by the 'field of play' doctrine; Morocco said it will pursue further legal avenues.
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld Senegal's appeal on Tuesday and reinstated its 1-0 win over Morocco in the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final. Morocco's federation said it would pursue all available legal avenues.
body: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on Tuesday that Senegal are the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions, setting aside a Confederation of African Football (CAF) appeal board decision that had awarded the title to Morocco.

The CAS statement said the CAF Appeal Board decision was set aside and the CAF Disciplinary Board decision reinstated. "Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed," it said. Senegal won the January 18 final in Rabat 1-0 after extra time.

The three-member panel was unanimous. It held that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala's decision to resume the match fell within his sole authority and was covered by the "field of play" doctrine, under which CAS generally does not review on-pitch decisions by match officials.

Senegal had walked off in second-half stoppage time to protest a penalty awarded to Morocco, causing a delay of about 15 minutes. After the players returned, Brahim Diaz's penalty was saved. Senegal scored the winner in extra time.

CAF's appeal board ruled in March that Senegal had forfeited the match and awarded Morocco a 3-0 win. Morocco had relied on Articles 82 and 84 of the tournament regulations. CAS said these apply only when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off a match permanently, which did not happen.

CAS acknowledged that the referee decided in extreme tension, but said this did not justify calling the decision arbitrary. CAS director general Matthieu Reeb said: "Both teams were on the pitch again and both expressed their willingness to resume."

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) said it "reaffirms its determination to pursue all available legal avenues". It said CAS had not considered recent positions of the International Football Association Board and FIFA on players leaving the field without the referee's authorisation.

The FRMF also expressed astonishment that CAS did not delay its verdict after the federation claimed that panel member Ulrich Haas had a private telephone call with the Senegalese federation's president on Sunday. CAS said a challenge commission found insufficient evidence to delay the decision. It said Haas strongly denies any direct contact with the parties.
The Senegalese federation posted: "Once again and forever, champions of Africa." Sadio Mané said on Instagram the decision "fills us with joy" and expressed solidarity with Morocco.
CAS rulings can be challenged at Switzerland's supreme court only on limited procedural grounds. The next men's Africa Cup of Nations starts in June, co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.
keyFacts: CAS panel's ruling in favour of Senegal was unanimous.
The final was played in Rabat on January 18; Senegal won 1-0 after extra time.
CAF's appeal board had awarded Morocco a 3-0 win in March.
CAS held an in-person, closed-door hearing in Lausanne in early October.

stories.whyItMatters: The ruling restores Senegal's title and confirms Morocco as runners-up, ending the dispute over who holds the continental championship unless a Swiss supreme court challenge succeeds.

stories.headline: Sinner has knee surgery, Australian Open return in doubt
stories.dek: The Italian, who has not played since winning Wimbledon in July, said his knee did not respond to treatment; no recovery timeline has been announced.
stories.summary: Jannik Sinner said on Tuesday he has had minor surgery on his right knee's iliotibial band, leaving his Australian Open return in doubt. The tournament's main draw begins on January 17; Sinner has not played since Wimbledon in July.
body: Jannik Sinner said on Tuesday he has undergone minor surgery on the iliotibial band in his right knee, putting his return at the Australian Open, which begins on January 17, in doubt.

The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played since winning Wimbledon on July 12. In a statement posted on Instagram, the 25-year-old said: "Over the past few months, together with my team, we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery."

He added: "After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we had all hoped, that's why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team." The Guardian reported that the operation was carried out by Finnish orthopaedic specialist Professor Lasse Lempainen.

No recovery timeline has been given. Italian daily Corriere dello Sport reported that Sinner could be out for as long as four months, according to Sportstar. The Guardian said the surgery seems almost certain to rule out a January comeback.

Earlier in November, Sinner said his aim was to travel to Australia and possibly play a few tournaments before the Grand Slam begins. A fortnight ago he said: "The aim is to go to Australia." He also said he had to respect medical protocols because rushing could cause more serious problems.

The Instagram post was the first time Sinner specified the nature of the knee problem. In an October video he said he had lost a lot of weight after having his tonsils removed, and described days when he could play without problems and days when he could not move at all.

Sinner has dropped to world number two. Alexander Zverev took the top ranking in his absence and won the US Open. Carlos Alcaraz, who won the ATP Finals on Sunday, is 350 ranking points behind Sinner, though he is defending 2,000 points in Melbourne.

Alcaraz told SuperTennis TV: "It's a shame we don't have Jannik. We really miss him." Sinner won the Australian Open in 2024 and 2025. Alcaraz is the defending champion, having beaten Novak Djokovic in the January final.

Sinner won 44 of his 47 singles matches in the first half of the season, including five consecutive Masters 1000 titles between March and May. He lost in the second round of the French Open, then won Wimbledon, beating Zverev in the final. Sportstar reported that he recently split with coach Darren Cahill and that Magnus Norman has joined his team.

The iliotibial band is a thick band of connective tissue along the outer thigh to the top of the shinbone.

stories.headline: PT Usha skips IOA nominations; Narang, Mehta and Sachdeva contest presidency
stories.dek: The incumbent did not file by Tuesday's deadline, leaving a three-way race for the Indian Olympic Association's top post in elections scheduled for December 5.
stories.summary: PT Usha did not file a nomination for the Indian Olympic Association presidency before Tuesday's deadline. Gagan Narang, Rajeev Mehta and Virender Sachdeva will contest the post in elections on December 5.
body: Incumbent P T Usha did not file a nomination for the Indian Olympic Association presidency before the deadline on Tuesday, leaving Gagan Narang, Rajeev Mehta and Virender Sachdeva in a three-way contest in the December 5 elections.

Narang, a 2012 London Olympics bronze medallist in shooting, is a current IOA vice-president. Mehta is a former IOA secretary and secretary of the Fencing Association of India. Sachdeva is secretary of the Archery Association of India and a Delhi BJP leader. The Hindu and Sportstar described Narang as a frontrunner. Football chief Kalyan Choubey is his proposer.

Sachdeva has also filed for the male vice-president's post, where boxer Vijender Singh is the other candidate. Usha is the proposer for Vijender and for Harjinder Singh, who is seeking a joint secretary's post.

Earlier this month, Usha failed to win a place among the eight Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elected to the IOA general assembly, The Indian Express reported. The Ice Hockey Federation of India then nominated her to the general assembly. Under the IOA constitution, a presidential candidate must either be elected by the SOMs or nominated by a national sports federation. The Telegraph reported that she exited after the SOM poll defeat.

Other contests are set. Kamlesh Mehta, a former table tennis player, is the lone treasurer candidate. Ajay Patel, the current senior vice-president, faces Mona Shah and Vagish Pathak. Anju Bobby George faces Bhavneet Handoo and Suman Kaushik for the female vice-president's post. Rani Rampal and Yogeshwar Dutt are set to join the Executive Council unopposed in the SOM quota.
Several members of the current council did not file, including treasurer Sahdev Yadav, Choubey and Saina Nehwal, one of the four elected SOM members.

The Indian Express reported concern over a perceived conflict between the IOA constitution and the election bye-laws. Article 14.1 of the constitution requires a candidate to win more than 50 per cent of valid votes, with a second round between the top two if no one does. Clause 3.4 of the bye-laws says the candidate with the most valid votes wins. Article 32 gives the constitution priority. "There could be legal challenges potentially, so there must be clarity over the voting procedure," a source told the paper.

The returning officer will vet the nominations. The last date for withdrawal is December 2 at 5 pm. The Hindu and Sportstar reported that the sports ministry and political circles want unanimous choices.

Last date to withdraw nominations is December 2 at 5 pm.

stories.whyItMatters: The IOA will have a new president to lead the body for the next four years, with several current Executive Council members absent from the contest.

stories.headline: Ramayana: Part 1 makes two Critics Choice shortlists, box office rises 28% on Tuesday
stories.dek: The film is shortlisted for visual effects and stunt design, while its third-Tuesday collection of ₹16.11 crore rose from Monday's ₹12.70 crore, according to Hindustan Times.
stories.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1 was shortlisted in two categories for the 32nd Critics Choice Awards, announced on Monday. Hindustan Times estimates its India net at ₹971.56 crore after a Tuesday rebound.
body: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, was shortlisted in the Best Visual Effects and Best Stunt Design categories of the 32nd Critics Choice Awards, the Critics Choice Association announced on Monday.

The shortlists cover 12 below-the-line categories. Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey leads with mentions in 11 of them. Dune: Part Three and the Spanish-language La Bola Negra have eight each, while Godzilla Minus Zero and Wildwood have seven each.

In visual effects, Ramayana is up against films including The Odyssey, Godzilla Minus Zero, Project Hail Mary and Spider-Man: Brand New Day, according to both Hindustan Times and The Indian Express. Dan Glass is credited for the film's visual effects, Hindustan Times reported. In stunt design, rivals include Dune: Part Three and The Odyssey.

The shortlists are not final nominations. Final nominations will be announced on December 4, with six films in each technical category. The Indian Express reported that members were expected to begin nomination voting on November 26. The ceremony is on January 3, 2027, hosted by Janelle James.

At the box office, Hindustan Times reported that the film earned ₹16.11 crore in India net on its third Tuesday, up about 26.85% from Monday's ₹12.70 crore. The headline of its report put the rise at 28%.
The Hindi version brought in ₹14.34 crore from 13,544 shows. Kannada earned ₹83 lakh, Tamil ₹58 lakh and Telugu ₹36 lakh. The estimated India net total stands at ₹971.56 crore.

The Indian Express, citing industry tracker Sacnilk, put the film's India net at Rs 955.45 crore, and said Monday was its steepest single-day drop. On that day the makers announced ticket prices starting at Rs 99, and many theatres showing the 2D version cut prices, some by nearly 50 per cent.

stories.headline: Karan Johar backs Deepika Padukone's eight-hour workday demand on Koffee with Karan
stories.dek: Akshay Kumar agreed with the filmmaker's view that disciplined, time-bound shoots benefit everyone on set, according to reports on the upcoming episode.
stories.summary: Karan Johar said on Koffee with Karan Season 9 that Deepika Padukone has earned the right to ask for an eight-hour workday. Akshay Kumar, who appears in the episode, agreed, according to Indian Express, NDTV and Hindustan Times.
body: Filmmaker Karan Johar has backed actor Deepika Padukone's demand for an eight-hour workday, saying on Koffee with Karan Season 9 that it is her right and that he does not know why it has become a big deal.

Akshay Kumar, who appears on the upcoming episode with actor-politician Ravi Kishan, agreed with Johar's view, the three outlets reported. They said Akshay backed an eight-hour shift model and said time-bound shoots benefit everyone on set without hurting creative output.

Johar began by praising Akshay's work habits. "Firstly, I've never seen a man work this hard. He has meetings at 5 am. He knows his script by heart, and he's always supportive of the director and very cognizant of the producer," he said. He added that Akshay is the only superstar who gives a chance to a debut director.

Johar then turned to Padukone. "As a producer, I respect it. And that's why I also respect Deepika Padukone's decision," he said. "She's a mother, she's a wife, she's a professional, and she has a personal life. Why can't she ask for it when you ask for it? There is sometimes this gender disparity that happens, and it's not fair."

He said any actor can ask for fixed hours, male or female. "Nobody's putting a gun on my head to sign Deepika Padukone or Akshay Kumar," he said. "I want to sign these actors because I love their work."
Hindustan Times reported that the two also pointed to Hollywood productions, from Tom Cruise's action films to Christopher Nolan's large-scale projects, as running on tightly planned schedules.

Reports in May 2025 said Padukone left Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Spirit after differences with the makers over working hours and other terms. Vyjayanthi Movies later said she would not be part of the sequel to Kalki 2898 AD because the two sides could not find a partnership.

Padukone has since addressed the issue. She told Brut India that many male actors have worked eight-hour shifts for years without it making headlines. She told CNBC-TV18 that if being a woman makes her seem pushy, "then so be it."
Padukone will next be seen in King, headlined by Shah Rukh Khan, which is due for release on December 24. The Koffee with Karan episode streams on JioHotstar on Wednesday at 7 pm.

stories.headline: Cine workers' body asks PM Modi to stop Netflix's Pakistani series in India
stories.dek: Netflix released the trailer for Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo on Tuesday and has not said whether Indian subscribers will be able to watch it.
stories.summary: The All Indian Cine Workers Association wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking a ban on Netflix's Pakistani series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo in India. Netflix released the trailer on the same day; the series premieres globally on December 4.
body: The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi asking him to stop the Pakistani series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo from streaming on Netflix in India, in a letter dated November 24.

The two-page letter is signed by AICWA President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta and was also marked to Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Netflix India. The association shared it on X on Tuesday.

AICWA listed four demands: that the series not be streamed in India on December 4 or later; that all OTT platforms strictly follow the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting's advisory of May 8, 2025; that the government bring a permanent law with penalties restricting Pakistani content, artists and productions on television, streaming platforms and in cinemas; and that Netflix India and other services state their position publicly.

The May 2025 advisory directed OTT platforms, streaming services and intermediaries in India to stop streaming Pakistan-origin content. The letter also referred to the 2019 Pulwama attack and the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam attack. AICWA argued that releasing the series would go against the spirit of the advisory and national sentiment.
In its post on X, the association said: "Pakistan was, is and will remain a terrorist country. Its series, films, songs, podcasts and all other content have no place on Indian screens."

Netflix released the official trailer on November 24, along with a six-song soundtrack, according to Hindustan Times. The series is based on Farhat Ishtiaq's Urdu novel and is Netflix's first original series set in Pakistan. It stars Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Sanam Saeed, Hania Aamir, Ahad Raza Mir, Iqra Aziz and Hamza Ali Abbasi, among others.

Netflix has not said whether the series will be available in India. Hindustan Times reported that as of November 24 it was visible on the Netflix India website but not on the app. Bollywood Hungama said the title had appeared in Netflix India's upcoming listings. NDTV said it had asked Netflix for comment.

NDTV reported that the posters drew criticism on social media, with some users citing past statements by cast members on India's strikes after Pahalgam. NDTV also noted that other users questioned whether a boycott would work. The series, titled All The Love Our Hearts Carry internationally, will be released in two parts, with Part 1 on December 4.

Calls to boycott Pakistani artists followed. The series is based on a novel first serialised in Khawateen Digest in 2009 and published as a book in 2013.

stories.headline: Marvel plans Patrick Stewart tribute in Avengers: Doomsday; India advance sales pass ₹57 crore
stories.dek: Director Anthony Russo says Stewart was struggling with his health on his last day on set, while Sacnilk figures show 9.13 lakh tickets sold in India.
stories.summary: Marvel Studios is working out how to honour Patrick Stewart in Avengers: Doomsday, Kevin Feige told Entertainment Weekly. In India, advance bookings have reached ₹57.71 crore with 9.13 lakh tickets sold, according to Sacnilk.
body: Marvel Studios is planning a tribute to the late Patrick Stewart in Avengers: Doomsday, studio president Kevin Feige told Entertainment Weekly, as advance sales in India passed ₹57 crore with 23 days to the film's release.

Stewart, who died on October 29 after a brief battle with Alzheimer's and Lewy Body Dementia, plays Charles Xavier in the film for the ninth and final time. Variety, citing the Entertainment Weekly feature, reported that he had been offered a role in the sequel, Avengers: Secret Wars, due in December 2027, but declined.

Feige said Stewart gave a speech to the crew on his last day of shooting. "We didn't know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was," he said.

Co-director Anthony Russo said it was clear Stewart was struggling with his health. "It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that," he said.

Feige said filming ended long ago and the team is now looking at "how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend." Co-director Joe Russo described Xavier as "the conscience in the movie" and said he shares a scene about forgiveness with Ian McKellen.

In India, the film has grossed ₹57.71 crore in advance bookings, including blocked seats, according to Sacnilk, as reported by The Indian Express. That figure comes from 9.13 lakh tickets across 8,025 shows as of 2 pm IST on Tuesday. Excluding blocked seats, the gross is ₹49.51 crore from 7.87 lakh tickets.

Opening day, Thursday, December 17, leads with ₹24.32 crore from 3.64 lakh tickets. The English version accounts for ₹48.42 crore, or 84% of the total, and the Hindi version for ₹7.37 crore. The National Capital Region is the biggest market at ₹9.86 crore, followed by Mumbai and Bengaluru.

The film will not screen in IMAX in India. Marvel has instead introduced a premium large-format experience called Infinity Vision, also available in 3D. The film opens in India on December 17, a day before its US release on December 18.

stories.headline: Dolly Parton's last recording with U2 debuts on three Billboard charts
stories.dek: 'Torn' gives Parton her highest Country Airplay debut and U2 its first country chart entries, as the band lists North American stadium dates for 2027.
stories.summary: 'Torn', the last song Dolly Parton recorded before her death, entered Billboard's country and rock charts, with firsts for both acts. U2 has also announced North American stadium dates running from August to October 2027.
body: Dolly Parton's final recording, 'Torn' with U2, has entered Billboard's country and rock charts dated November 28, giving Parton her highest-ever debut on Country Airplay and putting U2 on two country rankings for the first time, Billboard reported on Tuesday.

The song debuts at No. 39 on Hot Country Songs, Parton's first posthumous entry there. It drew 1.6 million official streams, 1.2 million in radio airplay audience and 6,000 sales from November 13 to 19, according to Luminate. On the Country Airplay chart dated November 21, it opened at No. 28.

On Hot Rock & Alternative Songs, 'Torn' enters at No. 24. That makes it Parton's highest-placed song on the tally, ahead of 'World on Fire', which reached No. 26 in 2023. It also starts at No. 2 on Billboard's all-genre Digital Song Sales chart.

'Torn' closes U2's album Carnaval De Luz, which debuts at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 with 49,000 equivalent album units. It is the band's 14th top 10. The album opens at No. 1 on Top Rock Albums, Vinyl Albums and Indie Store Album Sales.
The 12-track record, produced by longtime U2 collaborator Jacknife Lee, is the band's first album of new material in nine years and its 16th studio release.

According to Billboard, the song began when Parton offered U2 an unfinished piece of her own. Bono and Snow Patrol's Johnny McDaid reworked her story of a woman torn between two men into one about a mother and her two estranged sons, divided by political differences.
Parton recorded her vocals in Nashville in June while ill. She died on August 25 at the age of 80.

Separately, Pitchfork reported that U2 has added North American dates to its tour behind the album, named Carnaval De Luz Presents: The Greatest Show on Earth World Tour 2027. The stadium run spans August to October 2027, opening in Miami on August 13 and ending in Vancouver on October 18.

The War on Drugs will support the West Coast and Southern dates, and Stephen Wilson Jr. the East Coast shows. Earlier-announced legs take in Latin America, with Beck supporting, and Europe, with Wolf Alice, between February and July 2027.

stories.headline: Chiranjeevi to host Netflix talk show, teaser drops letter 'N' from his name
stories.dek: Netflix India says the premiere date for Chiranjeevi's Megaverse will be announced on November 30; the streamer has not named any guests.
stories.summary: Netflix released a teaser on Tuesday for Chiranjeevi's Megaverse, a talk show hosted by the Telugu star in his first outing as host. The promo shows his name missing the letter 'N' across a city until he supplies it.
body: Netflix on Tuesday released a teaser for Chiranjeevi's Megaverse, a celebrity talk show hosted by Telugu actor Chiranjeevi, who is making his debut as a talk-show host and his first collaboration with the streamer.

The promo opens with people on the street noticing that the letter "N" is missing from the name of "Megastar" Chiranjeevi on hoardings, autorickshaw posters, T-shirts, newspapers, murals and even a fan's tattoo, according to The Indian Express. A coconut seller, an autorickshaw driver and a girl on a date react with alarm.

The video then cuts to Chiranjeevi on a smartphone screen, seated in a red leather chair. He signals an "N" that resembles the Netflix logo to complete his name. "This is my territory," he says in Telugu, the line rendered as "Iddhi Na Adda", before a gangster-style laugh.

The teaser does not reveal the guest list or the premiere date. Netflix India told SCREEN that the date will be announced on Monday, November 30, according to The Indian Express. NDTV, citing a Deccan Chronicle report, said the show is expected to premiere on November 30 at 4:30 pm, but noted that Netflix has not confirmed this.

Netflix has not named guests. The Deccan Chronicle report, as cited by The Indian Express, said the line-up includes A-list names from several film industries, among them Kamal Haasan, Nagarjuna, Ravi Teja, Nani, Brahmanandam, Bobby and Sandeep Reddy Vanga.

Netflix describes the show as a mix of personal anecdotes, conversations and stories from Telugu cinema, with guests from cinema, sport and popular culture. "At its heart is Megastar Chiranjeevi, whose passion for cinema and deep-rooted connection with its people serve as the show's emotional anchor," a Netflix India statement said.

NDTV reported that the series is produced by Gold Box Entertainments, Atom Media Ventures and Sol Production LLP, and is being filmed. The caption on Netflix's post promised "Mega nostalgia, mega laughter, mega conversations".
On the film front, Chiranjeevi will next be seen in the action thriller Kaka, directed by Bobby Kohli, which is slated for release in cinemas on January 13, 2027, for Sankranti.
