stories.headline: Namma Metro Blue Line trials begin from KR Puram; public service targeted for mid-2027
stories.dek: Trains are running on the first four stations of the 19-km Phase 2A stretch, but signalling and safety certification remain pending, the minister said.
stories.summary: Trial runs have begun on the Namma Metro Blue Line from KR Puram, covering four stations on the Outer Ring Road corridor. Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said public operations are targeted for mid-2027, after signalling installation and safety certification.
body: Trial runs have begun on the Namma Metro Blue Line from KR Puram across the first four stations, with testing due to extend to another four stations next month, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Tuesday, November 24.
Gowda inspected the trials at Doddanekkundi station. He said public operations on the 19-km Phase 2A corridor, between KR Puram and Central Silk Board, are targeted for the middle of 2027.

Installation of the automatic signalling system is expected to take two to three months, he said. The government aims to finish it by January, with safety certification beginning after February. "Considering the testing and certification requirements, the entire process is likely to take another seven to eight months before the corridor is opened for public use," Gowda said.

The Times of India reported that the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (BMRCL) must also secure an independent safety assessment of the signalling system, testing by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation, and final authorisation from the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety.

The Phase 2A section has 13 stations. Gowda said an estimated 11-12 lakh people work along the Outer Ring Road, which he described as one of the city's most important employment and mobility corridors.

BMRCL managing director PC Jaffer said that getting a train on the mainline showed civil and track works were clear of major obstructions, which would help signalling work. Station work at Ibbalur and Silk Board is pending, and depot work at Byappanahalli is incomplete. BMRCL has received two trainsets from BEML, enough for the trials. BEML is due to supply 66 in all. Officials expect depot space constraints to ease by February.
BMRCL has not decided whether to open the 19-km stretch in phases or all at once. "Opening the line in phases is more challenging and requires almost the same effort and time," Jaffer said.

The full 58.2-km Blue Line, from Central Silk Board through KR Puram and Hebbal to Kempegowda International Airport, is estimated to cost around ₹20,000 crore. The government has set a target of completing it within 18 months. Gowda said work on the KR Puram-Hebbal stretch under Phase 2B needs to be accelerated.

On finances, Gowda said BMRCL records an annual loss of around ₹600 crore to ₹700 crore including depreciation, and an operating surplus of ₹50 crore to ₹60 crore excluding it. He said no decision had been taken on raising fares. He added that a weaker rupee had increased loan repayment costs, and that the state was releasing funds so that money does not delay expansion.
keyFacts: Trials cover the first four stations from KR Puram; four more stations are to be added next month.
The 19-km Phase 2A corridor has 13 stations, running to Central Silk Board.
Gowda said public operations could begin in about seven to eight months, targeted for mid-2027.
The full 58.2-km line to the airport costs around ₹20,000 crore, with an 18-month target.
BEML is to supply 66 trainsets; two have been delivered.
stories.background: Gowda said the need for metro connectivity along the Outer Ring Road was identified in 2016-17, when planning for Phases 2A and 2B began. The state cabinet approved the projects in 2017, proposals went to the Union government, and construction began in 2020.

stories.headline: Karnataka ASHA workers continue strike after CM's video appeal from Japan
stories.dek: Protesters at Bengaluru's Freedom Park say they will stay until Chief Minister DK Shivakumar visits and issues a written government order accepting their demands.
stories.summary: ASHA workers at Freedom Park rejected Chief Minister DK Shivakumar's video-call appeal to end their eight-day strike. They want a written order on a ₹15,000 monthly honorarium, while BJP state president B Y Vijayendra criticised the government.
body: ASHA workers in Karnataka refused on Tuesday to call off their indefinite protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru, rejecting an appeal by Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, made by video call from Japan, to give the government more time.

The agitation entered its eighth day. The protesters say they will not leave unless Shivakumar visits the site in person and issues an official government order accepting their demands, The Times of India reported. Many workers stayed on in cold weather and drizzle, some with toddlers.

Shivakumar, who is on an official visit to Japan, spoke to the workers' leaders. "Please allow us some time to work out a lasting solution. Your matter will be discussed during the Belagavi session. Kindly withdraw the protest," he said, referring to the coming winter session of the legislature.
The Indian Express quoted his statement as saying he would meet the workers after returning from Japan, discuss the matter with the finance department and "provide justice".

The workers are demanding that their monthly honorarium rise from ₹8,000 to ₹15,000. They also want pending dues released, retirement benefits of ₹5 lakh and better working conditions. The Indian Express put the number of protesters at about 41,000, camping at the site since November 17.

The workers say that in January 2025 then chief minister Siddaramaiah assured them of a rise to ₹10,000, but the May budget raised the honorarium by only ₹1,000. Sharadha, a protester from Bengaluru, said milk prices had risen by ₹8 a litre and asked how workers could survive on the increase.
More than 18 workers have been hospitalised since the protest began, the newspaper reported. A medical volunteer said several women had urinary tract infections, infected wounds and high fever.

The protest is led by the Karnataka State United ASHA Workers' Association, affiliated with AIUTUC, and has support from trade unions, activists and members of the film fraternity. Umamani of the Independent Union of Anganwadi Workers and Helpers said ASHA, Anganwadi and midday meal workers belonged to the same workforce.

BJP state president B Y Vijayendra criticised the government. He said the chief minister had claimed the treasury lacked ₹350 crore for ASHA workers but spent ₹100 crore of public money renovating his official residence. The government has not responded to that claim in the sources reviewed.
In a post on X on November 23, Vijayendra described the workers' demands as justified. He said the government had failed to give a satisfactory response.

Shivakumar said the issue would be discussed at the Belagavi winter session.

stories.headline: Speaker summons forest officials as Congress MLA withdraws elephant-row resignation
stories.dek: Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma kept her resignation in abeyance after talks with Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and party leaders, while the Forest Department's elephant drive continued.
stories.summary: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma withdrew her resignation over the Forest Department's elephant relocation drive after party leaders intervened. Speaker G S Patil has summoned forest officials over the row, Deccan Herald reported.
body: Speaker G S Patil has summoned Forest Department officials over the elephant relocation row, Deccan Herald reported on Tuesday, hours after Congress MLA Nayana Motamma withdrew her resignation over the drive.

Motamma, who represents Mudigere, had submitted her resignation to the Speaker's office on Monday. She was protesting the department's move to drive elephants from Hassan towards Chikkamagaluru district without consulting local legislators.

Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad said on Tuesday that he had spoken to her and advised against a hasty decision. He said Shivakumar and Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy had also held discussions with her and asked her to keep the resignation in abeyance until the issue is reviewed.
"This is not a matter that should lead to an immediate resignation. All of us must work together to find a solution to the problem," Hariprasad said.

The Times of India reported that three Congress MLAs from the district had threatened to quit: Motamma, T D Rajegowda of Sringeri and H D Thammaiah of Chikkamagaluru. It said Shivakumar, who is in Japan, phoned them and asked them to be patient until he returns. The paper said he reportedly assured them he had told officials to find a solution and temporarily halt the relocation. The Indian Express, citing sources, reported that the resignation letter had not been handed to the Speaker or the Assembly secretary and was not in the prescribed format.
Hariprasad said human-elephant conflict had killed 20 to 22 people in Chikkamagaluru in recent years and that the MLAs reflected local anxieties.

The drive, called Operation Gaja, began on November 16 after two people died in Belur taluk of Hassan district. According to the Indian Express, Hassan in-charge minister K M Shivalinge Gowda ordered it, saying Hassan lacks sufficient forest cover. The Chikkamagaluru MLAs said it was launched ahead of a consultation with Reddy.

On Tuesday, APCCF (Project Elephant) Manoj Rajan said four herds had regrouped into one group of 39 elephants about 3.5 km from Tatkola Reserved Forest in Mudigere taluk. He said staff were only facilitating the herds' natural movement. The Times of India reported that prohibitory orders were imposed in more than 50 Mudigere villages after the elephants entered the area.

Officials said the next stretch towards Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary, about 20-22 km, is planned by Thursday. Another group of 13 elephants is heading towards Belur. Reddy's meeting with legislators from Hassan and Chikkamagaluru has been rescheduled to November 30.

stories.headline: Madras HC calls it a 'sad day' as police book TVK MLA over collector's complaint
stories.dek: Justice V Lakshminarayanan said safeguards for women at work had failed and ordered an Internal Committee to report by November 27, with takedowns of social media posts.
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu police registered an FIR against Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh of the TVK after a woman IAS officer's complaint, the state told the Madras High Court. The court called it a 'sad day for the republic' and ordered an internal inquiry.
body: Tamil Nadu police have registered a first information report against Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam MLA C Arul Vignesh, who represents Kallakurichi, on a woman IAS officer's complaint of sexual harassment, the state public prosecutor told the Madras High Court on Tuesday.

The officer, a district collector, submitted a formal complaint on Monday, November 23, the prosecutor said. The Hindu, citing sources, reported that she handed it to the Superintendent of Police. Reports differ on the law invoked: The Hindu said the case was registered under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.

The allegations, as reported by The News Minute and The New Indian Express, include remarks about her clothes, inappropriate behaviour and an attempt to invade her personal space at an event about three months ago, and obscene WhatsApp messages. Vignesh has denied the allegations, calling them baseless and politically motivated.

Justice V Lakshminarayanan said it was "a sad day for the republic" that a district collector had to complain of sexual harassment. "Harassment does not choose time, place, monetary considerations or the status or office that a woman occupies," he said. He added that he shuddered to think what would happen to women in lesser posts.

The judge noted that the collector, as District Officer under the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (PoSH) Act, heads the district-level committee and could not approach it with her own complaint. NDTV reported that the State Public Prosecutor and Additional Public Prosecutor could not tell the court whether Tamil Nadu had a state-level committee. The court directed the state to constitute an Internal Committee to examine her grievance and report by November 27.

The court directed the cybercrime police to have existing social media posts on the case removed. It barred platforms and intermediaries from publishing material covered by the Act's confidentiality provisions until the committee finishes its proceedings, and said those violating them would face prosecution. It also directed the Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police to ensure notice is served on Vignesh.

On Monday, the court had been told that neither the Chief Secretary nor the police had received a complaint from the officer. The judge had said he would not interfere without one. The petition was filed by advocate R Thrishuli seeking an FIR and a fair investigation.

NDTV reported that the investigation has been given to a senior police officer from outside Kallakurichi, with an Inspector General-level officer monitoring it. Scroll, citing Live Law, reported that the court asked for a final report by December 22. The National Commission for Women has also taken suo motu cognisance and sought an inquiry by the director general of police.
The hearing was adjourned to November 27.
keyFacts: FIR registered after the collector's formal complaint on November 23, the state told the court.
Justice V Lakshminarayanan ordered an Internal Committee to report by November 27.
Vignesh denies the allegations, calling them politically motivated.
Police were asked to file a final report by December 22, Scroll reported.

stories.background: The allegations circulated on social media for months. The National Commission for Women took suo motu cognisance, and Madras High Court judge Justice Victoria Gowri made public remarks about alleged police inaction, NDTV reported. Some ruling TVK leaders asked why the officer had not filed a formal complaint.
stories.whyItMatters: The court's observations on the PoSH Act's committee structure bear on how women in senior and junior posts can seek redress at work in Tamil Nadu.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu to sign about 70 investment pacts at Chennai conclave
stories.dek: PepsiCo will break ground on an ₹800-crore packaged-food plant in Trichy district, and the state will lay foundation stones for projects worth about ₹8,000 crore.
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu is due to sign about 70 investment agreements worth more than ₹50,000 crore at the VETTRI conclave in Chennai on Wednesday. PepsiCo India will break ground on an ₹800-crore plant at Manapparai.
body: Tamil Nadu is due to sign about 70 investment agreements worth more than ₹50,000 crore at the second VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave in Chennai on Wednesday.

The figure differs by source. News18, citing Reuters and unnamed sources, put the total at over ₹50,000 crore. The Times of India reported that the memoranda of understanding were expected to involve more than ₹55,000 crore.

Royal Enfield and the German firm Vautid are among the companies expected to sign. News18 also named the Brazilian motor maker WEG. The sectors include manufacturing, industrial infrastructure, clean energy, engineering, textiles and electronics.

The state government will also lay foundation stones for projects worth about ₹8,000 crore and inaugurate six completed projects. Project activity is expected to extend beyond the traditional industrial clusters around Chennai to other regions.

PepsiCo India will break ground on a packaged-food factory at the SIPCOT industrial park in Manapparai, Trichy district. The company will invest more than ₹800 crore, in phases, according to company sources quoted by The Times of India.

The plant will make Lay's and Kurkure snacks and will be PepsiCo's first packaged-food factory in south India. Southern markets are now supplied from units in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh. A company source said the plant would raise local procurement of potato and corn.

The conclave will also include an update on MoUs signed since the TVK government took office. The Times of India reported that about three-fourths of roughly 113 MoUs signed over six months are understood to have reached the implementation stage.

Official figures released before the event, cited by News18, put the total at 112 pacts worth ₹1,14,812 crore across 23 sectors between May and November 2026. They are projected to create over 1.32 lakh jobs, and 83 of the projects have reached the land confirmation stage.
Industries Minister S Keerthana said: "Turning investment intent into working facilities and steady livelihoods is what matters most for our people."

The government wants to promote industrial development in Tirunelveli, Virudhunagar, Sivakasi and Dharmapuri, the Times of India reported. It plans plug-and-play industrial facilities at Gangaikondan and Tuticorin, and a digital land-allocation platform with 3D visualisation.
keyFacts: About 70 agreements worth more than ₹50,000 crore are due at the Chennai conclave on Wednesday.

Royal Enfield and Vautid are among the expected signatories.
stories.background: In August 2026, Tamil Nadu secured nearly 100 agreements worth ₹67,452 crore, News18 reported, with companies including Saint-Gobain and Super Micro Computer. Neighbouring Andhra Pradesh announced commitments earlier this month, including a ₹42,600 crore coal-to-gas project by Reliance Industries.
stories.whyItMatters: The pacts are meant to convert investment pledges into factories and jobs, and to spread industrial activity to districts beyond Chennai and Krishnagiri. The PepsiCo plant would bring packaged-food production for southern markets closer to consumers.

stories.headline: Chennai's northeast monsoon rainfall 29% below normal with days left in November
stories.dek: Meteorologists say the current easterly spell is unlikely to close the gap, and only a weather system could bring the rain needed.
stories.summary: Chennai has recorded 29% less rain than normal with less than a week of November left, and neighbouring districts show larger shortfalls. Meteorologists said the current easterly spell is unlikely to make up the deficit.
body: Chennai is facing a 29% rainfall deficit with less than a week of November remaining, and meteorologists said the current spell of easterly rain is unlikely to make up the shortfall, The Times of India reported.
Neighbouring districts are also short of rain. Chengalpet has a 50% deficit, Kancheepuram 43% and Tiruvallur 19%. November is Chennai's wettest month, with average rainfall of 37cm.
The India Meteorological Department has forecast moderate rain in Chennai and nearby districts until November 26. The easterly trough behind the spell has weakened and moved west, the report said.

V R Durai, director of the Area Cyclone Warning Centre at the Regional Meteorological Centre, Chennai, said supportive winds could still bring rain. Its intensity would vary across the city and suburbs depending on the trough's movement.

"The current spell may not help recover the deficit. Only a weather system can bring the rain needed to recover it. There is a possibility of a system developing in the first week of Dec, but models differ on its location," Durai said.
An IMD official said the trough may bring good rain to south Tamil Nadu and districts along the Western Ghats over the next few days, before it moves over Kerala.
For Wednesday, the city and suburbs may get moderate rain, with thunderstorms and lightning in some areas. Maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be 30–31°C and 23–24°C.

Statewide, moderate rain is likely on November 25 in northern and a few western and central districts, with heavy rain elsewhere. On November 26, heavy rain is forecast in four western districts and moderate rain in the rest of the state. Rain along north coastal Tamil Nadu may reduce to light intensity from November 27 to 30.
On Tuesday, Meenambakkam recorded 0.7mm and Hindustan University 4.5mm by 7.30pm. Monday's rain was heavier in the suburbs, with Injambakkam recording 7cm against 3cm in Nungambakkam.
keyFacts: Chennai's rainfall is 29% below normal with less than a week of November left.
Chengalpet has a 50% shortfall, Kancheepuram 43% and Tiruvallur 19%.
November is Chennai's wettest month, averaging 37cm of rain.
IMD forecasts moderate rain in Chennai and neighbouring districts until November 26.
A possible weather system in the first week of December has uncertain location, Durai said.
stories.background: The easterly trough is an elongated zone of low pressure that draws moisture-laden easterly winds together. The converging air rises, cools and condenses into rain-bearing clouds.
stories.whyItMatters: Chennai and three neighbouring districts are running below normal rainfall in what is usually the city's wettest month, and forecasters see no near-term spell large enough to close the gap.

stories.headline: Delhi police probe Jama Masjid station attacker for gang links; nine officers out of danger
stories.dek: Investigators are examining whether anyone instigated Nabeel, 30, who was shot six times in the legs after the Monday attack and is out of danger after surgery.
stories.summary: Delhi Police are investigating whether Nabeel, who allegedly stabbed police personnel at Jama Masjid station on Monday, had links to an organised gang. All nine injured personnel are out of danger, and police stations across the city have been told to tighten security.
body: Delhi Police are investigating whether a 30-year-old man who allegedly stabbed nine police personnel at and near Jama Masjid police station on Monday had links to an organised gang or was instigated by anyone, police sources said on Tuesday.

The nine injured personnel are out of danger, police said. The accused, Nabeel, was shot six times in the legs during his arrest, underwent surgery and is also stated to be out of danger. Once he regains consciousness, the Intelligence Bureau and other agencies are likely to question him jointly about his motive, sources said.

According to sources cited by Hindustan Times, Nabeel entered the station around 2.30 pm shouting "Who called me?" and attacked Sub-Inspector Arvind at the reception with a pocket knife. News18 put his arrival at about 2.57 pm. He had been summoned for counselling over a family dispute involving his mother and sister, who had approached police with a complaint.

The Times of India reported that he injured three more personnel who intervened, and that officers tried to shut the main gate on him. He fled after snatching a scooter, and police said five personnel were hurt inside the station.

Police formed teams from several stations, along with the Narcotics team and Special Staff, to find him. Appeals to the public produced leads within 15-20 minutes, according to the Times of India. He was cornered in the narrow lanes of Chitli Qabar between 4.15 pm and 4.30 pm, where he allegedly attacked four more personnel.
Police fired eight rounds, of which six hit him and two missed, sources said. Officers took care that no member of the public was hit.

Investigators have found no social media accounts belonging to him, Hindustan Times reported. News18 said police have so far found no evidence that anyone assigned him a target or directed the attack, and that his browsing and search history are being examined. Police are also checking for any history of drug use and whether he read material that may have influenced him.

Sources said he was unemployed and allegedly assaulted family members. The Times of India quoted an officer as saying he had attacked someone with a blade in 2022. Three cases have been registered, including two of attempt to murder, robbery and assault on police personnel. At least three of the injured may need plastic surgery, police sources told the paper.

Police stations across Delhi have been directed to strengthen security, and action will be considered against personnel found negligent, the Times of India reported. Officers it quoted suggested tasers, stricter entry checks and frisking, armed sentries and regular briefings. Another officer cautioned that tasers can have adverse health effects and that police stations must stay accessible to the public.

Nine personnel were injured; all are out of danger, police said.
Police fired eight rounds; six hit Nabeel in the legs.
Three cases have been registered, including attempt to murder and robbery.
Police stations across Delhi have been told to strengthen security.
stories.background: The Times of India recalled earlier attacks on Delhi Police personnel, including the stabbing of constable Kiranpal Singh in Govindpuri in November 2024 and a 2022 stabbing spree at Shahdara police station that injured five policemen and a home guard.
stories.whyItMatters: Police stations across Delhi have been told to tighten security, and officers have proposed changes to entry checks and equipment for personnel.

stories.headline: DJB collects ₹1,076 crore in old dues as ₹3,618 crore in surcharges waived
stories.dek: About 41% of eligible households and 26% of eligible commercial consumers have used the late payment surcharge waiver scheme, according to the Delhi Jal Board.
stories.summary: More than 5.66 lakh consumers have cleared pending water bills under the Delhi Jal Board's waiver scheme, Water Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh said. The board has collected over ₹1,076 crore in principal dues, while ₹3,618 crore in interest and surcharges has been waived.
body: More than 5.66 lakh Delhi Jal Board consumers have used the board's Late Payment Surcharge (LPSC) waiver scheme, with ₹3,618 crore in interest and surcharges written off and over ₹1,076 crore in principal dues collected, Water Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh said on Tuesday.

Under the scheme, consumers who pay the principal amount of unpaid water bills do not have to pay the surcharge that accumulated over the years. The Delhi government said the aim is to encourage consumers to clear long-pending dues voluntarily.
According to the Indian Express, 5.48 lakh of 13.39 lakh eligible households, about 41%, have availed the scheme. They paid ₹854.54 crore in principal and received waivers worth ₹1,886.89 crore.

Commercial consumers were brought into the scheme later. Of 70,312 eligible commercial consumers, 18,275, or about 26%, have used it. They paid ₹221.61 crore and received waivers worth ₹1,731.84 crore.

Households that availed the scheme outnumber commercial consumers by about 30 to one, yet the amounts written off are nearly the same. The Indian Express reported an average waiver of about ₹9.5 lakh per commercial consumer, against about ₹34,000 per household.

Singh, who is also DJB chairman, said consumers were coming forward voluntarily. "Our intention is not merely to recover dues, but to make it easier for every eligible consumer to settle their account and get the benefit of the rebate," he said.

The board is running an e-KYC drive to identify every eligible consumer. Singh said the aim is to complete e-KYC for all of them, extend the rebate and meet the target for recovering principal dues. The government has appealed to consumers who have not yet availed the scheme to complete their e-KYC.

The government said the recovered money would strengthen the DJB's finances and help improve water supply and sewerage services. Officials said the scheme, started earlier this year, will continue until August 15 next year.

stories.headline: CAQM tells Supreme Court NCR has 16,785 EV charging points for 12.94 lakh vehicles
stories.dek: The air commission's status report also says enforcement against end-of-life vehicles is 'far from satisfactory', with about 7% of 25.43 lakh such vehicles scrapped or moved out this year.
stories.summary: The Commission for Air Quality Management told the Supreme Court that Delhi and three NCR states have 16,785 EV charging points for 12.94 lakh electric vehicles. Delhi has 88.85% of them.
body: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has told the Supreme Court that Delhi and the three neighbouring NCR states have 16,785 electric vehicle charging points for 12.94 lakh electric vehicles, with Delhi holding most of them, according to its latest status report.

The commission said "vehicular pollution is one of the most significant contributing sectors to the generally poor air quality in Delhi-NCR". It said there is little infrastructure to support e-mobility.

Delhi had 14,913 operational charging points on October 31, 2026, for 6,83,251 EVs. That is 88.85% of the four-state total. Uttar Pradesh has 565 charging points for 3,47,587 EVs, Haryana 1,285 for 2,18,530 EVs, and Rajasthan 22 for 44,987 EVs.
The Supreme Court has recently observed that a large part of the capital's pollution is caused by vehicles entering Delhi from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan.

The Delhi government notified the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 on June 30, and it has been in effect since July 1. It requires new registrations of only electric L5 three-wheelers from January 2027 and only electric two-wheelers from April 1, 2028. It also sets phased electrification targets for commercial fleet operators, logistics aggregators and private schools.

The report said the other NCR states have been "advised" to revise their EV policies. The CAQM, represented by Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, acknowledged that e-mobility needs charging stations, battery swapping points and systems to dispose of large volumes of spent batteries.

On older vehicles, the report said 60.55 lakh of the 1,71,76,234 vehicles in Delhi-NCR meet BS-I to BS-IV standards, which it described as having "much higher polluting potential". Enforcement against end-of-life vehicles was "far from satisfactory" in Delhi and the NCR states, it said.

Of 25,43,679 end-of-life vehicles reported active across Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, nearly 1.86 lakh, a little over 7%, were scrapped or moved out of the region between January and October 2026. The commission noted that the apex court has barred coercive action against owners of over-aged vehicles.

Separately, Delhi's air quality was in the 'poor' category for the tenth consecutive day on Tuesday, with an AQI of 227, The Times of India reported. November has had 12 'poor' days, the most for the month since 2015, and no full 'severe' day. IITM data put vehicles' share of pollution at 15% on Tuesday.
GRAP Stage II measures remain in force. The Delhi government's winter curbs, which bar non-BS-VI vehicles registered outside the capital and private construction, run until January 31, 2027.

Delhi has 14,913 charging points, 88.85% of the regional total.
Rajasthan has 22 charging points for 44,987 EVs.
About 1.86 lakh of 25,43,679 end-of-life vehicles were scrapped or moved out in January-October 2026.
Delhi recorded 12 'poor' AQI days this November, the most for the month since 2015.
stories.background: The Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 has been in effect since July 1. The CAQM issued an advisory in May 2025 asking governments, public undertakings and institutions in NCR to procure or hire cleaner vehicles. The Union Finance Ministry had asked Union ministries to switch to EVs in December 2018.
stories.whyItMatters: The figures show charging infrastructure concentrated in Delhi while neighbouring states, whose vehicles enter the capital, have far fewer points per EV.

stories.headline: Only about 1,000 of 73.3 lakh excluded voters file fresh forms in Telangana
stories.dek: Telangana's chief electoral officer's office said district reports show only 50 to 100 people per district have submitted enumeration forms since the Election Commission offered another chance.
stories.summary: About 1,000 of the 73.3 lakh electors left off Telangana's draft roll have filed fresh enumeration forms, the state chief electoral officer's office said. Booth-level officers will collect forms until November 30, and the final roll is due on December 22.
body: Only around 1,000 of the 73.3 lakh voters left out of Telangana's draft electoral roll have submitted fresh enumeration forms since the Election Commission gave eligible electors another chance to be included, according to The Times of India, citing the state chief electoral officer's office.
The office said district reports showed that roughly 50 to 100 people in each district had come forward so far.

The largest group excluded from the draft roll published on August 17 was 45.1 lakh electors recorded as having permanently shifted from their registered addresses. Another 11.2 lakh were listed as absent or untraceable, 9.2 lakh as deceased and 6.7 lakh as already enrolled elsewhere.

Explaining how these entries were identified during the Special Intensive Revision, the CEO's office said: "This was done only after house-to-house visit and due enquiry by BLOs (booth-level officers) and not done unilaterally."

Election officials said many voters who found their names missing had already applied through Form 6 before the Commission offered the additional opportunity. Booth-level officers will collect fresh enumeration forms until November 30.

Separately, officials scrutinised 92.8 lakh electors on the draft roll whose records had drawn notices. District reports as of November 20 showed nearly 99%, or 92 lakh, had been cleared for the final roll. These included 60.1 lakh electors with logical discrepancies and 31.8 lakh whose entries could not be matched with earlier rolls.
Of the 2,64,87,213 electors on the draft roll, officials marked 2,63,96,341, or 99.6%, for inclusion. Another 58,772 were marked ineligible, and decisions were pending in 32,100 cases.
Hyderabad accounted for 22,958 of the pending cases, or 71.5% of the state total. Rangareddy had 29 pending cases and Medchal-Malkajgiri 22.
Rangareddy recorded the most electors marked ineligible at 13,493, including 11,471 unmapped voters. Mulugu had the highest proportion, at 1.39% of its draft electorate, against 0.22% statewide.
The final roll is scheduled to be published on December 22.

Electors on the draft roll whose records drew notices were scrutinised separately.

stories.headline: Vaishnaw's Metro Phase-II remark draws state-BJP sparring over Centre's support
stories.dek: Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao said the Congress government has no moral right to question the Centre's contribution to the state.
stories.summary: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw reportedly said he knew of no funding plan for Hyderabad Metro Phase-II, according to Swarajya. State BJP chief N. Ramchander Rao on Tuesday defended the Centre's role and criticised the Congress government.
body: Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said he is not aware of a funding plan for Hyderabad Metro Phase-II, according to a headline from Swarajya published on Tuesday, leaving the Centre's position on the project unclear.
The full text of the Swarajya report was not available, and the circumstances of Vaishnaw's remark are not detailed in the material reviewed here.

Later on Tuesday, Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao told reporters at the party's state office that the Congress government had no moral right to question the Centre's contribution to Telangana, The Hindu reported. He did not address the Metro project in the portions of his remarks reported by the newspaper.

Rao challenged state ministers to explain what they had delivered to each Assembly constituency during the government's three years in office. He claimed that some ruling party MLAs were complaining that development funds were being disproportionately allocated to Kodangal, the constituency of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy.

He said public turnout at padayatras led by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Hyderabad and BJP national president Nitin Nabin in Karimnagar showed growing support for the BJP. He said the party was well placed to form the next state government and could provide a corruption-free administration.

Rao also mocked the chief minister's prediction of winning 90 seats in the next election, saying the Congress could lose as many deposits. He criticised both the previous BRS government and the present Congress administration for failing to fulfil promises.

He further alleged that AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi was acting as an intermediary between the Congress and the BRS to curb the BJP's growth in Telangana. The sources do not carry responses from the Congress, the BRS or AIMIM.

stories.background: The Congress government led by A. Revanth Reddy has been in power in Telangana for three years. The BJP is positioning itself as an alternative ahead of the next Assembly elections, according to Rao's remarks.
stories.whyItMatters: Central funding decides whether and how fast Hyderabad Metro Phase-II can proceed, and the dispute shows the project's financing has become a political issue between the state government and the BJP.

stories.headline: Telangana to present ₹10,000-crore El Niño preparedness plan at climate conclave
stories.dek: Irrigation minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy said the five-month programme, to start after Sankranti, will be a main feature of the conclave at the Global Summit from December 7.
stories.summary: Telangana will present a proposed five-month, ₹10,000-crore El Niño preparedness programme at a climate conclave during the Global Summit at Bharat Future City from December 7. Irrigation minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy said works worth nearly ₹2,000 crore would be taken up each month.
body: Telangana will present a proposed five-month, ₹10,000-crore El Niño preparedness programme at a climate conclave during the three-day Global Summit, which begins on December 7 at Bharat Future City, Irrigation minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy said on Tuesday.

Reviewing preparations in Hyderabad, Reddy directed officials to keep the conclave focused on practical, scientifically proven solutions, with emphasis on drought resilience, water security, sustainable agriculture and readiness for El Niño conditions. He asked that globally recognised climate-resilience models, including best practices identified by ICRISAT, be built into presentations and audio-visual content.

“A major highlight of the conclave will be the govt’s proposed five-month El Niño preparedness programme worth Rs 10,000 crore, conceptualised by chief minister A Revanth Reddy. The programme envisages taking up works worth nearly Rs 2,000 crore every month after Sankranti in Jan,” the minister said.

The irrigation and panchayat raj departments will implement the programme jointly. It aims to rejuvenate tanks, streams and canals, improve groundwater recharge, expand rainwater harvesting and strengthen water conservation across rural Telangana. It is also expected to generate jobs during the agricultural lean season.

The presentations will set out the government's measures to protect drinking water supply and food security in a drought. Farmers are being encouraged to move from water-intensive paddy to alternative crops, so that reservoir stocks last until the next monsoon.
Reddy said the state has enough rice stocks to meet nearly one year's requirement under the public distribution system. He described this as a cushion against possible drought-related crop losses.

The conclave will also cover renewable energy expansion, industrial reuse of treated wastewater and steps towards Telangana's net-zero objectives. Officials noted that data centres in the state must already source at least 51% of their energy from renewable sources.

About 125 rural representatives, including sarpanches, are expected to join discussions on water security, climate resilience, biodiversity, urban heat management, agriculture and clean energy. Environmental experts, scientists, water conservation specialists and investors are also expected. An investor platform is planned for renewable energy, green credits, eco-tourism and the circular economy.
keyFacts: The Global Summit runs three days from December 7 at Bharat Future City.
The El Niño programme is worth ₹10,000 crore over five months.
Works worth nearly ₹2,000 crore are planned each month after Sankranti in January.
About 125 rural representatives, including sarpanches, are expected to attend.
Data centres in Telangana must source at least 51% of energy from renewables, officials said.
stories.background: El Niño conditions can affect monsoon rainfall and raise drought risk. The Telangana government says the programme was conceptualised by chief minister A Revanth Reddy and is still proposed, not yet under way.
stories.whyItMatters: The plan targets rural water bodies, groundwater and farm incomes in Telangana, and seeks to shift some farmers away from paddy to conserve reservoir water.

stories.headline: Keralam asks Centre to direct oil firms to supply pure petrol samples
stories.dek: Food and Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob says oil companies declined to hand over the reference samples laboratories need to check ethanol levels in fuel sold in the state.
stories.summary: Keralam's civil supplies minister has written to Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri seeking 100 per cent pure petrol samples for testing. The state says oil marketing companies refused to provide them, and results of its fuel tests are awaited.
body: Keralam's Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister Anoop Jacob has written to Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, asking him to direct oil marketing companies to supply 100 per cent pure petrol samples for testing ethanol content in fuel sold in the state.

Earlier this month, the state civil supplies department collected petrol samples from outlets of public sector firms. The Hindustan Times reported that the samples went to chemical examiner laboratories in three districts, to check whether ethanol content exceeded the permitted 20 per cent. The results have not yet been released.

Jacob said the laboratories told the department that cross-checking required pure petrol samples. "However, when we approached the oil marketing companies for the 100% pure samples, they were not provided to us. They claimed the samples were not available," he told reporters in Thiruvananthapuram.

In his letter, as reported by The Indian Express, Jacob said the samples are held only by firms such as IOC and BPCL. He said the companies had first agreed to supply them but later declined, and that repeated efforts by senior officials failed.

The minister said the exercise was not meant to undermine the credibility of oil companies. He said it aimed to address public apprehensions about the effect of ethanol-blended petrol on vehicle engines. "We want to test the samples the right way by following the standard procedure," he said.

Keralam took up the issue after Karnataka's Congress-led government alleged that petrol sold there exceeded the prescribed ethanol limit. Karnataka Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad cited private laboratory studies showing "31.2% ethanol blending in IOCL and 30.5% in HPCL." The Union government and the oil marketing companies rejected the finding and questioned how Karnataka collected and tested the samples.

Last week, Union Minister of State for Petroleum Suresh Gopi dismissed concerns about E20 fuel at Thrissur. He said India adopted E20 after extensive research and approval from the Automotive Research Association of India.
Neither report said whether Puri or the oil companies had responded to Jacob's letter.
keyFacts: Anoop Jacob wrote to Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri seeking pure petrol samples.
Samples were collected this month and sent to chemical examiner laboratories in three districts.
The permitted ethanol blend in petrol is 20 per cent.
Karnataka cited private lab results of 31.2% ethanol in IOCL and 30.5% in HPCL petrol.
Keralam's test results have not yet been released.
stories.background: India has moved to E20 petrol, which blends 20 per cent ethanol. Karnataka claimed its tests found higher levels, which the Centre and oil marketing companies rejected, questioning Karnataka's sampling and testing procedure. A 2014 Keralam notification empowers civil supplies officials to inspect fuel and initiate legal action under the 2005 Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel order.
stories.whyItMatters: The state says it cannot complete its tests of fuel sold to Keralam consumers without the reference samples. Public concern over the effect of E20 on engines is the stated reason for the testing.

stories.headline: Class IX student shoots classmate with revolver brought to Palakkad school
stories.dek: Police say the country-made weapon, taken from the boy's home, went off in a classroom at Parudur Higher Secondary School; the injured student is not in danger.
stories.summary: A Class IX student at a school near Thrithala in Palakkad district was injured on Tuesday when a classmate's unlicensed revolver went off in class. Police said the gun was brought from home and that a case will be registered against the boy's mother.
body: A Class IX student was injured on Tuesday when a country-made revolver brought to Parudur Higher Secondary School, Pallippuram, near Thrithala in Palakkad district, went off accidentally in a classroom, police said.

The Hindu reported that the incident took place at about 11.30 a.m. A classmate had brought the gun from home and was showing it to other students when it fired. NDTV quoted a senior police officer as saying the boy "brought the gun from home to show off and had no other motive."

The injured student is being treated at a private hospital at Kottakkal. The Hindu reported that he was shot in the armpit, while NDTV, citing the police officer, said he was shot in the bicep and was undergoing surgery to remove the bullet. The accounts differ on the exact site of the wound and on the treatment.

Doctors told The Hindu that the child was conscious, able to speak and had no life-threatening complications. The bullet remained lodged in his body, and doctors were testing for possible nerve damage along its path.

A ballistic examination found the seized weapon to be an improvised double-action revolver capable of firing 11 rounds, according to a preliminary report cited by The Hindu. It has no manufacturer's name or serial number but is in working condition.

Sub-inspector Sathyajith said school authorities told police the gun had been taken from a shelf at the student's home. Classmates told police the boy had been handling the weapon for some time, that rounds were loaded in it, and that it went off as he demonstrated its use.

Police said the gun had no licence. They are investigating its source, its ownership and how it reached the student, and whether the shooting was accidental. A case will be registered against the student's mother.

The school suspended classes and sent students home. Its management said bringing dangerous objects to school was prohibited, that checks would be strengthened, and that it would cooperate fully with police. It urged parents to remain vigilant.
General Education Minister N. Samsudheen directed the Director of General Education to investigate and submit an urgent report.
keyFacts: The shooting happened at about 11.30 a.m. on Tuesday at Parudur Higher Secondary School, Pallippuram.
Police say the revolver is improvised, unlicensed and can fire 11 rounds.
The injured Class IX student is conscious; doctors are checking for nerve damage.
A case will be registered against the shooter's mother, police said.
The education minister has sought an urgent report from the Director of General Education.
stories.background: Reports differ on the school's description: The Hindu named it a higher secondary school at Pallippuram, while NDTV called it a government school near Thrithala. Police said the type of gun and number of shots fired would be confirmed by firearms and forensic experts.
stories.whyItMatters: The case puts the focus on how a student carried a loaded, unlicensed firearm into a classroom, and the school has said it will tighten checks for dangerous objects.

stories.headline: BMC sends ₹37-crore digital classroom project to vigilance department for enquiry
stories.dek: Interactive panels installed in civic schools lack educational content, officials said, and 76% of the project cost has already been paid to the contractor.
stories.summary: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has referred its ₹37-crore digital classroom project to its vigilance department. Panels in several civic schools reportedly cannot be used for teaching because e-content has not been uploaded.
body: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has sent its ₹37-crore digital classroom project to the vigilance department for an enquiry, after interactive flat panels installed in several civic schools were found to lack educational content.
"We have sent the file to the vigilance department for enquiry," said Prachi Jambhekar, deputy municipal commissioner in charge of education, as quoted by The Times of India.

The project covers interactive flat panels (IFPs) meant to replace blackboards in 1,300 classrooms. It includes loading Maharashtra State Board e-content in Marathi, Hindi, Urdu and English medium for classes 1 to 10, along with CBSE, IB, ICSE and IGCSE syllabuses. The work order was issued roughly a year ago.

BMC education officials wrote in August to the suppliers, GurujiWorld Technologies Pvt Ltd and Eduspark International Pvt Ltd. They said the missing e-content prevented teaching through the panels. Officials said ₹28.2 crore, or 76% of the project cost covering hardware and content, has been paid to the contractor.

Last week, Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) demanded a probe and the blacklisting of the companies involved. Congress corporator and BMC group leader Ashraf Azmi and Shiv Sena (UBT) corporator Ankit Prabhu wrote to municipal commissioner Ashwini Bhide. They sought financial penalties, an immediate stop-payment, withholding of further payments and blacklisting proceedings.

The companies dispute the account. GurujiWorld Technologies said it is associated with the project only as an original equipment manufacturer of state board content and has completed all deliverables within its scope.

Eduspark said that it and its consortium partner had supplied and installed all 1,300 smart classrooms on time. In a statement it said prescribed content "has been supplied and installed across all 1,300 smart panels within the stipulated time frame". It added that it had assured the department of continued technical support, resolution of pending issues and completion of remaining teacher training.

Last month, Mumbai BJP president and MLA Ameet Satam alleged a nexus involving some education department officials. In a letter to mayor Ritu Tawde and Bhide, he asked BMC to provide students with tablets and digital panels from reputed global brands.
keyFacts: BMC has referred the ₹37-crore digital classroom project to its vigilance department.
The project covers interactive flat panels in 1,300 civic school classrooms.
Officials said ₹28.2 crore, or 76% of the cost, has been paid.
BMC wrote to GurujiWorld Technologies and Eduspark International in August about missing e-content.
stories.background: BMC launched the interactive flat panel project in 2025 to replace traditional blackboards in its schools. The Times of India reported that a year after the work order, e-content had not been uploaded in several schools.
stories.whyItMatters: Panels in several civic schools cannot be used for teaching, while most of the project's cost has been paid out.

stories.headline: Maharashtra FDA suspends 27 food licences, fines Mumbai University canteen ₹1 lakh
stories.dek: The same administration also cancelled the manufacturing licences of Pune-based Inducare Pharmaceutical for a second time, after two of nine unauthorised drugs were found spurious.
stories.summary: Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration suspended the licences of 27 food establishments in Mumbai and Pune and fined the Mumbai University canteen ₹1 lakh. It separately cancelled Inducare Pharmaceutical's drug manufacturing licences for the second time.
body: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the licences and registrations of 27 food establishments in Mumbai and Pune and fined the University of Mumbai's Fort campus canteen ₹1 lakh, it said on Monday, November 23.

Six of the suspended establishments are in Mumbai and 21 in the Pune division. The FDA said inspectors found pest infestations, improper food storage, inadequate waste disposal and missing food safety records. Banned food products worth ₹34.56 lakh were seized and four FIRs were registered during the statewide drive.

In Mumbai, the licence of British Brewing Company in Lower Parel was suspended on November 21. Inspectors reported live flies in a bag of flour, cockroaches near a drain clogged with food waste, and rusted utensils. The licence of the National Sports Club of India in Worli was suspended on November 23 after inspectors reported flies in the main kitchen, open dustbins near food preparation areas and food handlers working without gloves.

The FDA said the university canteen vendor was operating without a valid food business licence or registration. Inspectors reported food stored in ways that risked cross-contamination, utensils on the floor, open drains and no records of purchases, staff training, medical examinations or pest control. The fine was imposed and recovered.

Other Mumbai suspensions covered a Crusto's outlet in Prabhadevi, Velvet Fine Chocolates and Shane-Ilahi Bakery and Store in Govandi, and Maratha Chicken Suppliers in Borivali East. In Pune division, the list included Metro Restaurant, The Burger Barn Cafe, Chaitanya Parathas and an Instamart establishment operated by Rajdhi Retail Pvt. Ltd.

Separately, raids on banned products such as gutkha, pan masala and scented tobacco covered Mumbai, Amravati and Nashik divisions. The largest seizure, worth ₹34.53 lakh, was in Amravati division, where one person was arrested, two establishments were sealed and a vehicle valued at ₹21 lakh was seized.

On Tuesday, the FDA said it had cancelled the drug manufacturing licences of Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation, based in Jejuri, Pune district, for the second time. It said the firm made and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission, and government analysts declared all nine substandard, misbranded or spurious.

Two were found spurious. Ibucare Plus contained no ibuprofen, and the multivitamin Carevita-M contained none of the nine ingredients tested. The firm admitted in a written response that it had no separate product permissions, the FDA said. The order, issued on November 23, directs it to stop all manufacturing, packing, testing and distribution, and the FDA has proposed prosecution under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said: "Playing with public health will not be tolerated at all. Access to pure food is the right of every citizen." The FDA asked citizens to report suspected adulteration on its helpline, 1800222365, or its online grievance portal.
keyFacts: 27 food establishments suspended: six in Mumbai, 21 in Pune division.
Mumbai University's Fort campus canteen fined ₹1 lakh; it had no valid licence.
Banned food products worth ₹34.56 lakh seized; four FIRs registered.
Inducare's licences cancelled on November 23 over nine unauthorised drugs, two found spurious.
Earlier Inducare cancellation was on September 7; drugs worth ₹1.72 crore were seized from YCM Hospital.
stories.background: Inducare's manufacturing licences were first cancelled on September 7 after a joint inspection on July 14 and 15 found 25 serious deficiencies in Good Manufacturing Practices. About 13.86 lakh Caregyl-400 tablets had been made without mandatory batch records, and 5.20 lakh had been distributed. A sampled batch held only 32.44% of the claimed metronidazole. A show-cause notice followed on October 29, and a personal hearing was held on November 23.
stories.whyItMatters: Patients and diners are directly affected: the FDA said the drugs were distributed, including to a Pimpri-Chinchwad hospital's store, and the food outlets serve the public daily. The licensing authority said treatment-failure risk exists even without patient complaints.

stories.headline: West Bengal to be renamed Paschim Banga, resolution due in Assembly on December 9
stories.dek: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said the name will be written exactly as 'Paschim Banga' in English, with the resolution then going to the Centre.
stories.summary: West Bengal's Cabinet has cleared a proposal to use 'Paschim Banga' as the state's name in English, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said. A resolution will be tabled in the Assembly on December 9, as the Congress questions a wider renaming exercise.
body: A proposal to rename West Bengal as 'Paschim Banga' will be tabled in the State Assembly on December 9, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Monday, November 23, after a Cabinet meeting at the State Secretariat.

"West Bengal will be known as 'Paschim Banga' in English as well. The name must be written exactly as 'Paschim Banga'. We will introduce a resolution in the Assembly on the 9th. After its passage, it will be sent to the Government of India for the necessary parliamentary and legal procedures," Adhikari said.
The state is already called 'Paschim Banga' in Bengali. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government wants the same name used in English and other languages, The Hindu reported.
Adhikari said the formation of West Bengal has a history dating back to June 20, 1947, and that this history must be recognised.

The BJP's state leadership has often said the word 'Paschim Banga' is part of the history of the state's creation. West Bengal bore the brunt of Partition, and its eastern part became East Bengal, now Bangladesh. The party has also pointed to the role of Shyama Prasad Mookerjee and others in seeking the state as a homeland for Bengali Hindus during Partition, according to The Hindu.

On June 20, the BJP government observed Paschimbanga Divas. The date marks the day in 1947 when Mookerjee, the Jana Sangha founder, moved a proposal in the Bengal Legislative Assembly to partition Bengal.

The renaming is part of a wider set of changes. The Hindu's explainer refers to the renaming of Kolkata's streets. The Telegraph reported that Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned a change to the name of an airport, and that the paper carried a reminder about Jawaharlal Nehru in the context of the renaming spree. The full text of that report was not available.

The previous Trinamool Congress government passed a resolution in July 2018 to rename the state 'Bangla'. The Union government did not act on repeated requests from Mamata Banerjee's government to make that change official.
After the Assembly vote on December 9, the resolution will go to the Government of India.

The English name is to be written exactly as 'Paschim Banga'.
The Trinamool government's July 2018 resolution for 'Bangla' was not acted on by the Centre.

stories.whyItMatters: If the Centre approves, the state's official English name would change from West Bengal to Paschim Banga, a name the BJP links to the history of Partition.

stories.headline: Bengal makes prime-time Bengali film show compulsory in cinemas
stories.dek: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari met film industry representatives at Nabanna on Tuesday, a day after makers of 'Sadhak Bamakhyapa' said they could not get screens.
stories.summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari told film industry representatives that every cinema hall must show at least one Bengali film in prime time. The meeting followed complaints from the makers of 'Sadhak Bamakhyapa' about a shortage of screens.
body: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said at a meeting with film industry representatives in Nabanna on Tuesday, November 24, that every cinema hall in the state must show at least one Bengali film during prime time.

The Times of India reported that Adhikari said there is no restriction on screening films in other languages, but a prime-time slot must be ensured for Bengali films. He also expressed dissatisfaction over the recent dispute about 'Sadhak Bamakhyapa' not getting the required number of shows.

On Monday, November 23, the makers of the film had said they could not secure halls across the state. Actor Saheb Chattopadhyay said he was not against films in other languages, but that Bengali films should not be pushed out for national and international releases.

Actor and BJP MLA Rudranil Ghosh said one Bengali film would have to be shown in prime time "under any circumstances", and that special care would be taken to ensure Bengali films are not suddenly removed from shows. Roopa Ganguly, also an actor and BJP MLA, said financial approval had been given for many halls.
Ghosh said new theatres would be built at 51 locations and 70 old halls would be converted into cinema halls. Producer-distributor Anjan Bose said all 56 subdivisions would soon have one cinema each.

According to the Times of India, the chief minister asked for a committee of producers, distributors and exhibitors to address screen-sharing issues of mainstream and independent Bengali cinema. Exhibitor Arijit Dutta, owner of Priya, said a footfall recorder would be installed at all theatres, and that the government would explore ways to cover any shortfall if a Bengali film did not earn adequate revenue.

Dutta disputed the account given to the chief minister. "This film was not taken off any theatre where it was running," he said, asking why the information had been shared wrongly. Navin Chowkhani, owner of Navina, said three shows of 'Ramayan' were playing there this week and he would now screen one show of 'Sadhak Bamakhyapa' in prime time.

Actress Rituparna Sengupta called the discussion "very positive". She said a prime-time decision had been taken earlier too, and that this time the emphasis was on implementing it. Producer Shrikant Mohta said the industry could look completely different five years from now if all sides worked together.
After the meeting, the BJP's West Bengal social media account said 'Sadhak Bamakhyapa' would not be sidelined and would be screened across the state.
keyFacts: Meeting held at Nabanna on Tuesday, November 24, with chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.
At least one Bengali film must run in prime time in every cinema hall.
A committee of producers, distributors and exhibitors is to be set up.
Rudranil Ghosh said new theatres would come up at 51 locations.
Footfall recorders are to be installed at all theatres, exhibitor Arijit Dutta said.

The Times of India reported that exhibitors disputed parts of that account, and Rituparna Sengupta noted that an earlier prime-time decision already existed.

stories.headline: Bengal CM Adhikari tells traders to cut mustard oil and sugar prices at once
stories.dek: At a meeting at Nabanna Sabhaghar, he also ordered police to act against hoarding; trader bodies said producers and manufacturers set prices.
stories.summary: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari told traders' organisations on Tuesday to immediately lower the prices of mustard oil and sugar. Trader bodies said prices are largely set by producers and manufacturers, not traders.
body: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday asked representatives of traders' organisations to bring down the prices of mustard oil and sugar immediately, The Times of India reported.

He chaired a meeting at Nabanna Sabhaghar with trader bodies, wholesalers and officials of the agricultural marketing department to review prices of essential commodities. The Times of India said he reportedly told the traders that the government was cooperating with wholesalers and retailers but was not seeing a matching effort to ease prices for ordinary people.

Adhikari also asked the organisations to play a more active role in keeping potato, vegetable and other staple prices within reach of consumers. He directed police and administrative officials to take stringent action against traders involved in illegal hoarding and in artificially restricting supply to push up prices.

Sources at Nabanna told the newspaper that departments concerned have been told to meet traders' organisations every Monday to review market prices and start corrective steps. A secretary-level WhatsApp group will be formed for real-time coordination. Officials said the government wants a sustained surveillance mechanism rather than occasional interventions, and may carry out market inspections if necessary.

Official data and market reports cited by the newspaper show prices have climbed. In August, mustard oil in Kolkata rose from Rs 160 to Rs 180 per kg, and sugar from Rs 45 to Rs 65 per kg. By the end of October, mustard oil was selling at about Rs 200. Union consumer affairs department data for November 22 put Bengal's retail prices of packaged mustard oil at Rs 229.50 per litre and sugar at Rs 67 per kg.

Some vegetable prices have also risen sharply after crop damage from successive cyclonic disturbances. Between November 13 and 23, brinjal went from Rs 40 to Rs 100 per kg, pumpkin from Rs 20 to Rs 45, and tomatoes from Rs 30 to Rs 50.

Trader bodies rejected the blame. Sushil Poddar, president of the Confederation of West Bengal Trade Associations, said: "The prices of commodities, whether edible oils, sugar or other staples, are largely determined by producers and manufacturers, not traders." He said traders work on thin margins and have limited control over pricing.
Poddar said he has asked the chief minister to attend a proposed traders' conclave as chief guest, so that traders can explain the supply chain and the constraints they face.
keyFacts: Adhikari chaired the meeting at Nabanna Sabhaghar on Tuesday.
Union data for November 22 put Bengal's packaged mustard oil at Rs 229.50 per litre.
Sugar retailed at Rs 67 per kg in Bengal on November 22, per the same data.
Officials are to meet traders every Monday to review prices.
Police have been told to act against hoarding and artificial supply restrictions.
stories.background: The Times of India linked the chief minister's message to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks at FICCI's annual convention in New Delhi on November 19, where Modi questioned whether businesses were sharing the benefits of tax relief with ordinary citizens.
stories.whyItMatters: Households in Bengal are facing higher costs for cooking oil, sugar and vegetables, while traders face possible inspections and police action over hoarding.
